name: Irregular Verbs
ko: 규칙에 따르지 않고 활용이 달라지는 동사·형용사(ㅂ·ㄷ·르 불규칙 등)를 묶어 부르는 분류.

name: 간
meaning: Follows expressions of time (초, 분, 시간, 며칠, 년 etc), indicating that an action continued throughout a period.
examples: 묻지마 방화가 일어나는 바람에 지하철 운행이 30분간 중단되었다.
여자친구랑 헤어지고 나서 며칠간 술에 취해 펑펑 울었어요.
ko: 시간어(초·분·시간·년 등) 뒤에 쓰여 그 기간 내내 동작이 계속되었음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Due to an unprovoked arson, the subway did not run for 30 minutes.
That politician actually worked as a middle school teacher for 9 years, starting in 2009.
After my girlfriend broke up with me, I spent several days drunk and crying.
example_zh: 因无端纵火，地铁停运了30分钟。

name: 같이
meaning: Indicates resemblance or a metaphorical comparison in actions or objects
ko: 둘 이상이 함께함을 나타내거나, 앞말과 비슷함을 비유할 때 쓰는 조사.
example_en: She is as pretty as you.
Walk like a robot.
He is handsome like a actor.
example_zh: 她像你一样漂亮。

name: 경
meaning: Follows time words like '시,' '분,' '월,' '반,' to express that an event or action occurred around that time.
examples: 시현에 따르면 어젯밤 8시경부터 친구와 해변에서 불꽃놀이를 했다고 한다.
ko: '시·분·월·반' 등 시간어 뒤에 쓰여 그 무렵의 시점을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: It would have been around April last year.
Minsu headed for the train station at 1 or so.
According to Sihyeon, she was setting off fireworks with her friend on the beach starting last night at about 8.
example_zh: 大概是去年4月左右吧。

name: 까지
meaning: Indicate the end of the range of time, place or action.
examples: 전화비 많이 나오게 언제까지 떠들고 있을 거야!
ko: 시간·장소·동작의 범위가 거기서 끝남을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: I will work until 6 o'clock today.
I should wait until it cools down a bit.
Until when are you going to keep talking and make the phone bill go up!
example_zh: 今天我要工作到6点。

name: 껏
meaning: to that capacity’s fullest extent.
examples: 시험이 끝났으니 이제 마음껏 놀 수 있어요.
ko: 할 수 있는 만큼 최대한까지 이루어졌음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I want to rest to my heart's content on the weekend.
Now that the exam is over, I can finally play as much as I want.
Let’s run as hard as we can today.
example_zh: 周末我想尽情地休息。

name: 께
meaning: Define a person or a living creature as the recipient or target of an action. This is the honorific version of 한테 or 에게.
ko: 동작을 받는 사람을 높여 나타내는 조사로, '에게/한테'의 높임말.
example_en: I greeted the teacher.
I sent the report to the boss.
example_zh: 我向老师问了好。

name: 께서
meaning: Mark the subject of the sentence. The honorific version of 이/가.
ko: 주어를 높여 나타내는 조사로, '이/가'의 높임말.
example_en: What is my father reading?
The boss gave presents to the employees.
example_zh: 父亲在看什么呢？

name: 끼리
meaning: Used to indicate that actions or interactions are done among members of the same group or category.
ko: 같은 무리끼리 서로 행동함을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: The friends watched a movie together.
The kids are playing together at the playground.
The students are sharing opinions among themselves.
example_zh: 朋友们一起看了电影。

name: 네
meaning: Shows which group a person is part of
ko: 사람이 속한 무리나 집단을 나타내는 접미사(예: 우리네).
example_en: Minsu's store always has many customers.
Suji's family went on a trip.
We had a party at my friend's house.
example_zh: 民洙的店总是客人很多。

name: 님
meaning: An honorific particle designating people, showing them respect and honor.
ko: 사람을 높여 가리키거나 부를 때 붙이는 존칭 접미사.
example_en: I heard that the man who lives next door is a teacher.
The boss is going on a business trip.
Sir/Madam, this is a new product.
example_zh: 听说住在隔壁的大叔是老师。

name: 답다
meaning: Indicate that it has some of the qualities or characteristics of the noun and turn it into an descriptive verb.
ko: 명사 뒤에 붙어 그 성질을 띤 형용사를 만드는 접미사(예: 사랑답다).
example_en: They acts like a gentleman.
He is like a general who won the war.
example_zh: 他的行为真有绅士风度。

name: 당
meaning: Typically follows measure words, creating a ratio between a measure word and a value. Similar to 마다.
examples: 그 드라마는 회당 시청률이 80%를 넘을 정도로 아주 핫했어요.
할인주차권의 유효시간 종료 이후에는 10분당 1,000원의 할증요금이 부과됩니다
ko: 단위마다 어떤 수치가 해당함을 나타내는 조사(예: 한 명당).
example_en: The hot dogs are 5,000won each.
That drama was so popular that its viewership rate per episode was over 80%.
Once the parking voucher expires, an additional charge of 1,000won will be imposed per 10 minutes.
example_zh: 热狗一个5千韩元。

name: 당하다
meaning: To be the -- often helpless -- subject of an action, performed by someone else, that has a negative consequence for the subject.
examples: 조금 바보 취급당하는 것 같아서 기분이 좋지는 않았다.
악플 많이 달면, 차단당할 수도 있어요.
자연사는 절대 아니었을 거예요. 저는 언니가 살해당했다고 믿습니다.
학교에서 담배를 파는 게 들켜서 퇴학당했어요.
ko: 남의 행동으로 피해를 입음을 나타내는 접미사(예: 버림당하다).
example_en: I asked out the girl I liked and got rejected.
It felt like I was being treated as though I were stupid, so I didn't feel good.
If you leave a lot of hate comments, you may get blocked.
She absolutely did not die of natural causes. I believe she was murdered.
I got expelled after getting caught selling cigarettes at school.
example_zh: 向喜欢的女生告白后被拒绝了。

name: 대로
meaning: When added to the end of a noun, it indicates that something is "as" or "in accordance with" the noun.
ko: 앞말의 내용 그대로임을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: Everything is proceeding as planned.
Just as the appearance on screen, that actor is stylish.
example_zh: 一切都按计划进行着。

name: 더러
meaning: Follows a pronoun or title to define a person as the recipient or target of an action. Commonly used with expressions related to speech or conversation.
ko: 말이나 행동이 향하는 사람을 가리키는 구어적 조사.
example_en: Ask my brother about that.
Who said you smell bad?
I'm not telling you to just put up with everything.
example_zh: 那个事你去问哥哥。

name: 도
meaning: It indicates that the noun is being added to a list of items, actions, or descriptions previously mentioned or understood from the context.
ko: 이미 말한 것에 다른 것을 더하거나 극단을 강조하는 보조사.
example_en: I actually don't have confidence yet either.
The friend came too.
example_zh: 其实我也还没有把握。

name: 되다
meaning: Indicates nouns into passive verbs, things working out, becoming something.
ko: 어떤 상태로 변하거나, 명사를 피동·사동 동사로 만드는 표현.
example_en: I was selected for the baseball team!
My grammar mistakes were corrected.
A new policy was proposed in the National Assembly.
Don't worry. It will work out.
Caterpillars become butterflies.
Is it allowed to take pictures here?
example_zh: 我入选棒球队了！

name: 드리다
meaning: Attaches to nouns denoting action and expresses that the action is done respectfully.
ko: 행동을 공손하게 함을 나타내는 표현으로, '주다/말하다' 등을 높여 씀.
example_en: You must first greet your parents.
Thank you, teacher!
example_zh: 首先要向父母请安。

name: 들
meaning: Attached to nouns, pronouns, adverbs, etc. to indicate plurality.
ko: 둘 이상임을 나타내는 복수 접미사.
example_en: Did you fight with the kids next door?
I cut the fruits beautifully and put them on a plate.
We invited Mina's close friends to our house.
example_zh: 和隔壁的孩子们打架了吗？

name: 따라
meaning: Follows a time expression and expresses that some action happened exclusively or unusually so in that period of time and does not represent the usual behavior or state of affairs.
ko: 앞에 말한 시기나 상황에 맞추어 그대로 이어짐을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: Why's the weather like this today?
My husband came home unusually early that day...
example_zh: 今天天气怎么这样？

name: 랑/이랑
meaning: Connects multiple nouns, indicating a list or group without specifying order.
ko: 여러 명사를 나열하거나 함께함을 나타내는 구어적 조사.
example_en: Sir, please give me a bread and twisted doughnuts.
example_zh: 老板，请给我面包和麻花。

name: 랑/이랑
meaning: Indicates that an action involves more than one party or that something is done together with someone or something else.
ko: 여러 명사를 나열하거나 함께함을 나타내는 구어적 조사.
example_en: Did you get into a fight with the guys in the next room?
Let's try solving it together with the teacher.
example_zh: 和隔壁房间的孩子们吵架了？

name: (으)로
meaning: Expresses the means or tools that enable us to perform an action.
ko: 수단·도구·방향·자격 등을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: I go by bike.
I write with a pencil.
example_zh: 我骑自行车出行。

name: (으)로
meaning: Used to express a direction.
examples: 우리 집 창밖으로 서울 타워가 보여요.
ko: 수단·도구·방향·자격 등을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: You can see the Seoul Tower from the window of our house.
example_zh: 从我们家的窗外能看到首尔塔。

name: (으)로써
meaning: This form shows how something happens or is done using a certain method or way.
ko: 어떤 수단이나 방법으로 일이 이루어짐을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Cut the meat into pieces with a knife.
The students solved the problem through discussion.
example_zh: 用菜刀把肉切成块。

name: 마다
meaning: When preceded by a temporal indication, it indicates the recurrence of an event.
ko: 일정한 간격이나 단위마다 반복됨을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: Check every 3 hours.
My stomach hurts every time I eat.
example_zh: 请每3小时确认一次。

name: 마다
meaning: Indicates the inclusion of all the elements of a group with no exception.
ko: 일정한 간격이나 단위마다 반복됨을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: Each country has a different flag.
The Fire Nation goes to war every day.
example_zh: 每个国家的国旗都不同。

name: 마따나
meaning: Used with the word 말 to express sentiments like "as you said", "as mentioned", "as I say", "as you say".
examples: 자네 말마따나 극과 극은 통하는 법이지.
ko: '말'과 함께 쓰여 '말한 대로'라는 뜻으로, 상대의 말에 공감을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: As you said, I think I'd better get some rest.
Just as you said, opposites attract.
example_zh: 正如你所说，还是休息一下比较好。

name: 마저(도)
meaning: Emphasizes that the additionally included listed item is least expected.
examples: 집에 너무 늦게 오니까, 강아지마저 잠들어 있었어요.
ko: 나머지까지 모두 포함됨을 강조하는 보조사.
example_en: Even my family doesn't believe me.
Even hope has disappeared.
Because I came home very late, even the dog was asleep.
example_zh: 连家人都不相信我。

name: 만
meaning: A particle that expresses the sense of limitation, emphasis and degree of comparison.
examples: 제 남동생은 액션 영화만 보고 다른 영화는 안 봐요.
주말에는 하루 종일 집에서 잠만 자요.
ko: 한정하거나 비교의 정도를 나타내는 보조사.
example_en: My younger brother only watches action movies and doesn't watch other movies.
On weekends, I just sleep at home all day.
example_zh: 我弟弟只看动作片，不看其他电影。

name: 만큼
meaning: When added to the end of a noun, it describes something done as much as the noun.
ko: 앞말에 해당하는 정도임을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Our house is as quiet as a park.
It's as scary as seeing a ghost.
example_zh: 我们家像公园一样安静。

name: 밖에
meaning: Express the only thing or option available, no other possibilities available.
examples: 왜 빵을 두 개밖에 안 줘?
ko: 그것뿐이고 다른 선택지가 없음을 나타내는 표현(뒤에 부정어가 옴).
example_en: This is the only blue-green marble in the world.
Why are you only giving me two pieces of bread?
He knows nothing but studying.
example_zh: 蓝色的地球在世界上只有一个。

name: 받다
meaning: Attaches to nouns denoting action and expresses that the subject is the recipient of that action.
ko: 명사 뒤에 붙어 그 행동을 받는 쪽임을 나타내는 동사.
example_en: Hyunwoo is loved by everyone.
I got praise from the teacher.
example_zh: 贤宇深受大家的喜爱。

name: 보고
meaning: Used to indicate the person to whom a question, request, order, etc is directed at. Commonly used in colloquial speech when quoting others.
examples: 회선 씨가 세훈 씨보고 보고서 쓰는 설 도와 달라고 하던데요.
남편이 저보고 보라색이 잘 어울린다고 했어요.
ko: 질문·명령 등이 향하는 상대를 가리키는 구어적 조사.
example_en: Heesun asked Sehun to help write the report.
My husband told me that purple suits me.
example_zh: 熙善让世勋帮忙写报告。

name: 보다
meaning: Express that something is more or less than the noun in a certain quality or quantity. Used to directly compare two items.
ko: 비교의 기준이 되는 대상을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: Taxis are faster than buses.
More than anything, people need love.
example_zh: 出租车比公交车快。

name: 부
meaning: Indicate the starting point of an action, time or place.
ko: 어떤 일이나 시간의 시작점을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: The new regulation takes effect as of July 1.
She left the company as of last Friday.
This agreement becomes effective as of tomorrow.
example_zh: 新规定自7月1日起施行。

name: 부터
meaning: Indicate the starting point of an action, time or place.
ko: 시간·장소·동작의 시작점을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: I will start now.
The festival will be held from the 23rd.
The subway runs from 5 a.m.
example_zh: 现在开始。

name: 뿐
meaning: Used when there is nothing more than the content of the preceding statement or when it is the only one.
examples: 하루 종일 먹은 게 김밥 한 줄뿐이라서 너무 배가 고파요.
ko: 그것뿐이고 다른 것은 없음을 나타내는 보조사.
example_en: I'm so hungry because I only ate a piece of kimbap all day.
I only have a thousand won.
example_zh: 一整天只吃了一条紫菜包饭，肚子好饿。

name: 스럽다
meaning: Indicate that it has all of the qualities or characteristics of the noun and turn it into an descriptive verb.
ko: 명사 뒤에 붙어 그 성질을 띤 형용사를 만드는 접미사(예: 자연스럽다).
example_en: The puppy smiles in such a lovable way.
The teacher is so old-fashioned.
example_zh: 小狗笑得非常可爱。

name: 시키다
meaning: Indicates causation or making someone do something.
ko: 남에게 어떤 행동을 하도록 시킴을 나타내는 사동 접미사.
example_en: The boss made the employees work.
Today I made my younger sibling clean the living room.
Dad turned off the computer and forced me to study.
I was so hungry so I ordered pizza.
example_zh: 老板让员工们干活。

name: 씩
meaning: Emphasis that something is being done or distributed equally among people or things.
examples: 저희 가족은 매주 일요일마다 한 번씩 영화를 보러 가요.
ko: 똑같이 나누어지거나 조금씩 변화함을 나타내는 보조사.
example_en: Please distribute one book to each student.
My family goes to watch a movie once every Sunday.
I am learning little by little.
example_zh: 请给学生们每人分一本书。

name: 아/야
meaning: A casual form of address used for things like juniors, friends, and animals.
examples: 야, 이 멍청아! 제대로 공부 안 해?
ko: 친한 사이나 아랫사람을 부를 때 쓰는 호격 조사.
example_en: Hey, you idiot! Won't you study properly?
Bird, bird, bluebird.
Cheolsu, where are you going?
Hey guys, come here!
example_zh: 喂，你这个笨蛋！不好好学习吗？

name: 어치
meaning: Used to mean the amount that corresponds to that price
examples: 그의 경험은 매우 값어치 있는 것이었다.
ko: 그 값에 해당하는 분량을 나타내는 조사(예: 천 원어치).
example_en: I bought 20,000 won worth of books at that store.
His experience was very valuable.
example_zh: 我在那家店买了两万韩元的书。

name: 에
meaning: Indicates the time of the action. Can be used with days, hours, seasons, etc.
ko: 동작이 일어나는 시간을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: The plane leaves at nine o'clock.
I caught a cold last week.
example_zh: 飞机9点出发。

name: 에
meaning: When used with 있다 or 없다, it express the location of a person or thing.
examples: 집에 안 쓰는 나무판자나 널빤지 같은 거 없나?
zh: 在……（处所，与 있다/없다 连用）
ko: 있다·없다와 함께 쓰여 사람이나 사물의 위치를 나타내는 조사.
example_en: There is a cat on the sofa.
Do we have any unused wooden boards or planks that we don't use at home?
example_zh: 沙发上有只猫。

name: 에
meaning: When used with verbs of movement, it express the direction of the action.
ko: 이동 동사와 함께 쓰여 동작의 방향을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: Go sit in the empty seat over there.
My younger sister goes to school, my younger brother goes to kindergarten.
example_zh: 去那边的空位坐吧。

name: 에게
meaning: Define a person or a living creature as the recipient or target of an action. This is the formal version of 한테 or 께.
examples: 저는 친구에게 빌려준 책을 달라고 했어요.
경찰이 운전자에게 운전면허증을 보여 달라고 해요.
ko: 동작을 받는 사람이나 대상을 나타내는 조사('한테'의 격식체).
example_en: I asked my friend for the book I lent him.
The police ask the driver to show his driver's license.
example_zh: 我让朋友把借给他的书还给我。

name: 에다가
meaning: Shows where something is put or added.
ko: 무엇을 놓거나 더하는 장소를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I put the laptop on the table.
I put rice into the bowl.
Put the books into the box.
Write your name on the paper.
I put soy milk in the fridge.
Where did you put the pen?
example_zh: 我把笔记本电脑放在桌子上了。

name: 에서
meaning: Used to indicate where an action occurs or to indicate a reference frame that is considered a point of origin.
ko: 동작이 일어나는 장소나 기준이 되는 출발점을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: Is it far from Seoul?
I studied for 5 hours at the self-study room.
Who do you like the most among us?
example_zh: 离首尔远吗？

name: 와/과
meaning: Connects multiple nouns, indicating a list or group without specifying order.
examples: 초가집에는 어머니와 어린 삼 남매가 살았다.
ko: 여러 명사를 이어 주거나 함께함을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: In the straw-thatched house lived a mother and her three young siblings.
Taiwan and Japan are on good terms.
example_zh: 茅草屋里住着母亲和三个年幼的兄妹。

name: 와/과
meaning: Indicates that an action involves more than one party or that something is done together with someone or something else.
ko: 여러 명사를 이어 주거나 함께함을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: You and I are friends for the rest of our lives.
I went with my friend.
example_zh: 你我是会相伴一生的朋友。

name: 요
meaning: Used to indicate respect for the other person, the subject who is shown respect.
ko: 말 끝에 붙어 상대에 대한 공손함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I was smelling the scent of flowers.
example_zh: 我刚才在闻花香。

name: 요
meaning: Used when you have a response related to the question by using '요' as the short answer. A way to reply with just a noun, without having to repeat any of what has just been said. Also written as 이요.
ko: 말 끝에 붙어 상대에 대한 공손함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Where are you going? Seoul Station.
Son, what did you eat for lunch? Ramen.
How many people are you making a reservation for? 10 people.
example_zh: 您去哪儿？首尔站。

name: (으)로서
meaning: Indicates the role, capacity, or status of someone or something in relation to an action or state.
ko: 자격이나 신분을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: You must fulfill your responsibilities **as a student**.
I am doing my best **as a parent**.
He attended the meeting **as a representative**.
**As a secretary**, I provide accurate information.
I want to help you **as a friend**.
I'll give you advice **as a colleague**.
example_zh: 作为学生要尽到自己的责任。

name: 은/는
meaning: Mark the topic of the sentence
ko: 문장의 주제를 나타내는 보조사.
example_en: I am a student.
The chameleon's tongue is as fast as lightning.
Sugar is sweet like candy.
example_zh: 我是学生。

name: 을/를
meaning: The object marker is used to indicate that a noun is the object in a sentence.
ko: 문장에서 목적어임을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: I have been waiting for 10 years since then.
I have also gone several times.
example_zh: 从那时起等了10年。

name: 의
meaning: Used to express a relationship between two words, which can be expressed as "of" in English. The first noun being the possessor of the second noun.
ko: 앞 명사가 뒤 명사의 것임을 나타내는 관계 조사.
example_en: Friend's house.
When is your younger sister's birthday?
I felt the shaking of the earthquake.
example_zh: 朋友的家。

name: 이/가
meaning: Mark the subject of the sentence.
ko: 문장의 주어임을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: The snow is falling heavily.
If your hair is long, you should tie it up.
example_zh: 雪下得很大。

name: (이)나
meaning: Can be used to list two or more choices and one of them will be chosen. V+거나 is the same but with verbs.
examples: 학교 갈 때는 버스나 전철을 타고 갑니다.
ko: 둘 이상의 선택지를 나열하고 그중 하나를 고를 때 쓰는 조사.
example_en: When I have free time, I either read books or watch movies.
When going to school, I take the bus or subway.
example_zh: 有空的时候我看看书或看看电影。

name: (이)나
meaning: It expresses that the amount of something is much more than expected or higher than the standard.
ko: 수량이 예상보다 훨씬 많거나 기준보다 높음을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: I have as many as five younger brothers.
example_zh: 我有五个弟弟呢。

name: (이)나
meaning: It expresses that the choice is not really one's first choice but it is fine as the second best option.
examples: 오늘 오후에 시간 있으면 카페에나 갑시다.
ko: 첫 번째 선택은 아니지만 차선으로 괜찮음을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: If you have time this afternoon, let's, at least, go to a cafe.
example_zh: 今天下午有空的话，至少去趟咖啡店吧。

name: 이다
meaning: Express that the subject and predicate are the same thing.
ko: 앞말이 뒷말과 같음을 '~이다'로 서술하는 표현.
example_en: I am a student.
Today is my friend's birthday.
example_zh: 我是学生。

name: (이)라도
meaning: It expresses the speaker's choice of something will suffice even though it may not be the best choice.
examples: 배가 고파서 라면이라도 먹어야 될 거예요.
ko: 최선은 아니어도 그것으로 만족할 수 있음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Do you want some snack <f>at least</f>?
I'm so hungry, I should <f>at least</f> eat ramen.
example_zh: 要不要吃点零食？

name: (이)랍시고
meaning: Expresses that someone is pretending or acting as if something is something, often with a mocking or critical tone.
examples: 그는 의사랍시고 조언을 했지만 도움이 되지 않았다.
ko: ~라고 뻔뻔스럽게 내세움을 비꼬아 나타내는 표현.
example_en: He pretended to be a doctor and gave advice, but it wasn't helpful.
He claimed to be a friend but deceived me.
He pretended to be an expert and explained, but he was wrong.
The child, pretending it was a gift, gave me a lollipop.
example_zh: 他自以为是医生似的提了建议，但没什么用。

name: (이)시여
meaning: A polite form of address, often implying an exclamation or an appeal. This is a more polite version of (이)여.
ko: 높이거나 정중하게 부르며 탄식·애원할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Almighty God, have mercy on us.
O God please watch over us.
example_zh: 全能的主啊，请赐予我们慈悲。

name: (이)야
meaning: Express that the subject and predicate are the same thing.
ko: 주어와 서술어가 같음을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: Now is break time.
example_zh: 现在是休息时间。

name: (이)야
meaning: Particle referring to an emphasis.
examples: 커피야 늘 한 잔씩 마시고 있어.
ko: 앞말을 강조하는 조사.
example_en: I always have a cup of coffee.
Why are you just getting here now?
example_zh: 咖啡我总是每天喝一杯。

name: (이)야말로
meaning: Emphasizes the preceding noun as the prime example among a number of other possibilities.
ko: 여러 가운데 대표적이거나 두드러진 것을 강조하는 표현.
example_en: Hangul really is the best alphabet in the world.
I think exercise is the most important thing.
example_zh: 韩文正是世界上最优秀的文字。

name: (이)여
meaning: A polite form of address, often implying an exclamation or an appeal.
ko: 정중하게 부르며 감탄이나 호소를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Lord, forgive me for my sins.
Young people, make the most of your time.
My fellow countrymen, wake up!
example_zh: 主啊，请宽恕我的罪过。

name: 이자
meaning: Indicate that someone or something is both A and B simultaneously.
ko: 앞말과 뒷말이 동시에 해당함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: He is both my teacher and friend.
She is both an actress and a singer.
This book is both a textbook and a reference book.
Seulgi is a programmar as well as a woman.
This place is both a tourist spot and a historical site.
example_zh: 他既是我的老师，也是我的朋友。

name: 이자
meaning: Emphasize that someone or something is both the first and the last
examples: 그 사람은 우리 나라의 처음이자 마지막 공주였어요.
이 경기는 그의 처음이자 마지막 출전이었다.
ko: 앞말과 뒷말이 동시에 해당함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: That person was our country's first and last princess.
This match was his first and last appearance.
This is my first and last chance.
example_zh: 那个人是我国第一位也是最后一位公主。

name: 조차
meaning: Used to emphasize that something is not even as much as something else. An inclusion of extreme cases that are generally hard to predict. The one attached to 조차 is the most important.
examples: 그 학생은 시험마다 공부조차 하지 않은데 성적표가 진짜 대단하네.
ko: 극단적인 경우까지 포함됨을 강조하는 보조사.
example_en: Even my mom doesn't believe me?
That student doesn't even study for exams, but their grades are really amazing.
example_zh: 连妈妈都不相信我吗？

name: 짜리
meaning: Something of such a number or amount
ko: 그 수나 값에 해당하는 것임을 나타내는 접미사(예: 천 원짜리).
example_en: Do you have these shoes in size 6?
My house is a three-story building.
example_zh: 这种鞋有6码的吗？

name: 째
meaning: Follows nouns, including time nouns and counters, to express that a noun is the nth occurrence of something.
examples: 세 번째 노크 후에 문이 열렸다.
병원에 근무한 지 6년째 되던 해에 연인이 생겼다.
고등학교 때부터 이 공포증을 이겨낼 여러 가지 시도를 해봤어. 상담 선생님도 두 명째야.
ko: 순서나 횟수를 나타내는 접미사(예: 세 번째).
example_en: The door opened after the third knock.
There hasn't been a single customer for 30 minutes.
In her 6th year working at the hospital, she got into a relationship.
Since high school, I've tried many times to overcome this fear. I'm on my second counselor, too.
example_zh: 敲了三次门后，门开了。

name: 쯤
meaning: Used after nouns indicating numbers, quantities, and time to express approximation.
examples: 저는 일 년에 두 번쯤 여행을 가요.
ko: 수량이나 시간의 어림을 나타내는 조사.
example_en: I arrived at the airport around one o'clock.
I travel about twice a year.
example_zh: 我1点左右到了机场。

name: 처럼
meaning: Expresses similarity or metaphor, can be translated as "like" in English
ko: 앞말과 같거나 비슷함을 비유하여 나타내는 조사.
example_en: Sugar tastes sweet like candy.
Salt tastes salty like sea water.
A chameleon's tongue is as fast as lightning.
example_zh: 糖像糖果一样甜。

name: 치고
meaning: Used to show that something is unusual or noteworthy
examples: 그는 학생치고는 김치를 정말 잘 담가요.
이 가게는 동네 식당치고는 인테리어가 굉장히 세련됐네요.
이 옷은 디자이너치고는 꽤 평범한 편이에요.
ko: 다른 것과 비교했을 때 두드러짐을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: For a student, he makes kimchi remarkably well.
For a neighborhood eatery, this place’s interior is remarkably stylish.
For a designer piece, this outfit is quite plain.
For a physicist, she is surprisingly emotional.
For a health food, this salad is surprisingly sweet.
example_zh: 作为学生来说，他腌的泡菜真的很好。

name: (은/는)커녕
meaning: Used typically in negative sentences in the form 'A는커녕 B', meaning that not only did a negative event A happen (or a positive event A did not happen), but that an even more negative event B happened (or a less positive event B did not happen either).
examples: 그 시절 운동은 커녕 하루의 절반은 누워 있었다.
1999년에 지구 멸망은커녕 멀쩡하게 잘 돌아가고 있었다.
시험을 망친 진우에게는 위로의 말을 해주기는커녕 오히려 차갑게 대했다.
가해자가 피해자를 불러내 돈을 돌려주지 않으면 죽여 버리겠다며 식칼로 협박을 했는데, 피해자가 겁을 내기는커녕 바보 취급하듯 비웃었어요.
ko: A는 말할 것도 없이 B 정도도 못함을 나타내는 표현(주로 부정문과 함께).
example_en: Yugyeong wasn't able to attend elementary school, much less college.
Back then, not only did I not exercise, I spent half of each day lying down.
Not only did the world not end in 1999, everything was going just fine.
Not only did I not comfort Jinwoo after he failed his test, I treated him coldly.
The perpetrator met the victim and said he would kill her if she didn't return his money, threatening her with a kitchen knife, but the victim mocked him without showing any sign of fear.
example_zh: 有京别说上大学，连小学都没能上。

name: 하고
meaning: Connects multiple nouns, indicating a list or group without specifying order.
ko: 여러 명사를 이어 주거나 함께함을 나타내는 구어적 조사.
example_en: I bought books and magazines.
I quit smoking and drinking.
example_zh: 我买了书和杂志。

name: 하고
meaning: Indicates that an action involves more than one party or that something is done together with someone or something else.
examples: 그 사람이 싫은 건 아니고 그냥 저하고 성격이 잘 안 맞는 거 같아요.
ko: 여러 명사를 이어 주거나 함께함을 나타내는 구어적 조사.
example_en: I had dinner with my colleague yesterday.
It's not that I don't like that person, but I think our personalities don't match well.
example_zh: 昨天和公司同事吃了晚饭。

name: 하다
meaning: Turns nouns into action verbs, turns nouns into descriptive verbs, to perform actions, to do something.
ko: 명사를 동사나 형용사로 만들어 행위를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I do yoga every morning.
That company sponsored the event.
How will you solve this problem?
This trip will be special.
That singer is famous.
We decided to do the meeting at 3 PM.
I'll do that task.
example_zh: 我每天早上做瑜伽。

name: 한테
meaning: Define a person or a living creature as the recipient or target of an action.
examples: 뭐라고? 야 꼬맹이 너! 지금 나한테 한 소리야?
ko: 동작을 받는 사람을 나타내는 구어적 조사.
example_en: I sent a gift to my friend.
To whom did you give that money?
What did you say? Hey, you little brat! Are you talking to me right now?
example_zh: 我给朋友寄了礼物。

name: 는/(으)ㄴ/(으)ㄹ
meaning: Enables it to function as a modifying clause for the substantive following it.
examples: 우리는 일요일 아침에 늦잠 자는 것을 좋아합니다.
ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며 주는 관형형 어미.
example_en: There is a beautiful flower garden around the lake.
Let's prepare the food to eat in the evening.
We like to sleep in on Sunday mornings.
example_zh: 湖边有美丽的花园。

name: (은/ㄴ/는)데
meaning: Used by the speaker to provide some background information to the listener so they can understand the context.
examples: 신발이 조금 작은데 더 큰 사이즈 있어요?
음식이 너무 매운데 물을 좀 더 넣어 주시면 좋겠어요.
ko: 상대가 상황을 이해하도록 배경을 제시하며 말을 이어 주는 연결 어미.
example_en: My shoes are a little small. Do you have a bigger size?
The food is too spicy. Could you add more water?
example_zh: 鞋子有点小，有再大一点的尺码吗？

name: (은/ㄴ/는)데
meaning: It can be used to express the expectation for a response from the listener.
ko: 상대가 상황을 이해하도록 배경을 제시하며 말을 이어 주는 연결 어미.
example_en: Today is a bit busy...
My head hurts a lot.
example_zh: 今天有点忙……

name: (으)ㄴ/는지
meaning: Indicate an ambiguous, uncertain reason or judgment about the following statement. Can also indicate a vague doubt.
examples: 시험 문제가 어려웠는지 점수가 좋은 학생이 적어요.
제 친구는 여행을 좋아하는지 방학 때마다 여행을 가요.
ko: 앞 내용이 불확실한 이유나 근거가 됨을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: Fewer students scored well because the test questions were difficult.
My friend goes on a trip every vacation, so I think she likes traveling.
example_zh: 可能是因为考试题太难，得高分的学生很少。

name: 거나
meaning: Used when one of either the preceding statement or the following statement can be chosen.
examples: 저는 주말에 책을 읽거나 영화를 봐요.
주말에는 공부를 하거나 밖에서 놀거나 합니다.
ko: 앞뒤 내용 중 하나를 선택할 수 있음을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: I read books or watch movies on weekends.
On weekends, I either study or go out.
example_zh: 我周末读书或看电影。

name: 거늘
meaning: Used to express a reason or cause, often implying a contrast or rhetorical question.
examples: 경고를 받았거늘 또 같은 실수를 하다니.
ko: 앞 내용이 근거가 되어 뒤 내용으로 이어짐을 나타내는 문어체 연결 어미.
example_en: Considering that he worked hard, why did he fail?
Even though it's spring, the weather is still cold.
Considering that you were warned, you made the same mistake again.
example_zh: 他那么努力，为什么会失败呢？

name: (이)거니
meaning: Not only the first clause is true, but the second clause is also true.
ko: 앞의 사실을 인정하면서 뒤의 사실을 덧붙이는 연결 어미.
example_en: He is not only kind but also wise.
The weather is not only cold but also very windy.
This food is not only delicious but also affordable.
She is not only a student, but also a writer.
example_zh: 他不仅善良，而且富有智慧。

name: (이)거니
meaning: Used to affirm or emphasize a past event or truth before stressing the following statement.
examples: 그녀가 바빴거니 더 이상 기다리지 않았어요.
zh: 先承认过去的事实，再强调后句
ko: 지난 일이나 사실을 인정한 뒤 뒤의 말을 강조하는 어미.
example_en: Yes, I was wrong, and I have regrets about it.
Yes, she was busy, so I didn’t wait any longer.
example_zh: 是啊，是我不对，我很后悔。

name: (이)거니
meaning: Indicate repetitive or alternating actions.
ko: 동작이 반복되거나 번갈아 일어남을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: People come and go to the gathering.
example_zh: 人们来来去去参加聚会。

name: 거든(요)
meaning: Referring to the reason, cause, or basis for the preceding statement that the speaker thought of. Usually expected that the listener has no prior knowledge of the reason. Used only in conversation.
examples: 오늘은 공부해야 해요. 내일 중간시험을 보거든요.
시원한 바람이 솔솔 불고, 배가 고프면 간식도 먹을 수 있거든요.
한국에서는 집의 크기를 이야기할 때 '평', 평이라는 단위를 쓰거든요.
ko: 앞말에 대한 이유나 근거를 설명하는 종결 어미.
example_en: I have to study today. Because I have a midterm exam tomorrow.
The cool breeze is blowing, and if you're hungry, you can also eat snacks.
In Korea, when talking about the size of a house, we use the unit called '평'.
example_zh: 今天得学习，因为明天有期中考试。

name: 거든(요)
meaning: Express that if the preceding statement turns out to be true, then the following statement can happen.
ko: 앞의 말이 사실이라면 뒤의 일이 일어남을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: If you're busy, please go first.
Shall we play soccer when the rain stops?
example_zh: 要是忙的话，请先走吧。

name: 거들랑/걸랑
meaning: Indicates the speaker is revealing information the listener is likely unaware of.
examples: 사실은 그 아이가 내 친구 동생이걸랑.
ko: 상대가 모를 만한 정보를 알려 줄 때 쓰는 어미.
example_en: We were living in Seoul around then.
Actually, that kid is my friend's younger sibling.
example_zh: 那时候我们住在首尔。

name: 거들랑/걸랑
meaning: Expresses that if the preceding statement turns out to be true, then the following statement can happen.
examples: 커피가 마시고 싶걸랑 설탕을 사 와라.
ko: 앞의 말이 사실이라면 뒤의 일이 일어남을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: If you see Chul-soo, please give him my regards.
Write me if you go to Seoul.
If you want coffee, go buy some sugar.
example_zh: 如果见到哲洙，请转达我的问候。

name: 거라, 너라
meaning: Used to give commands. Old-fashioned compared to -아라/어라/해라. NOTE: -너라 has the same meaning, but is used exclusively with -오다 verbs.
examples: 지금 당장 교실로 가거라. 선생님이 기다리신다.
ko: 아랫사람에게 명령할 때 쓰는 옛말 어미(너라는 '주다'에 쓰임).
example_en: Eat quickly.
Take your time hanging out before you go.
Go to your classroom immediately. Your teacher is waiting.
Come out quickly.
example_zh: 快吃吧。

name: 건
meaning: Used in everyday conversations to offer choices in a casual way.
examples: 커피 마실래? 커피건 차건 다른 음료 마시고 싶은 거 있어?
주말에 영화 보러 가건 집에서 쉴 거야.
매운 음식 좋아해? 짜건 단 건 어때?
직접 만나건 전화로 얘기하건 편한 방법으로 하자.
친구들을 만나건 혼자 있건 오늘은 기분 좋게 지낼 거야.
ko: 고를 수 있는 대상을 나열하는 구어적 표현(-거나의 준말).
example_en: Do you want a coffee? Or would you like tea or something else?
This weekend, I'll either go see a movie or just rest at home.
Do you like spicy food? How about salty or sweet?
Whether you're meeting in person or talking on the phone, do it in a way that's comfortable for you.
Whether I'm with friends or alone, I'll be in a good mood today.
example_zh: 要喝咖啡吗？还是想喝点茶或别的饮料？

name: 건대
meaning: Expresses that the clause that comes after is something that the speaker has heard, seen, or wishes or believes. Commonly added to verbs like "장담하다," "짐작하다," "보다," "바라다."
examples: 장담하건대 그 친구가 분명히 시험을 잘 볼 것이다.
지금까지 받은 보고를 종합적으로 판단해 보건대 부검 할 필요는 없을 것 같습니다.
추측건대 이 실험실에서 탈출하려면 초록문을 열어야 해.
말투로 짐작건대 지금 아내와 사이가 별로 안 좋은 것 같다.
ko: 앞 내용이 화자의 소망이나 확신임을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I swear to you, I didn't do it.
I can assure you that he/she will do well on the test.
Based on a comprehensive look at the reports I've received up until now, there should be no need to perform an autopsy.
Judging by his/her intonation, he/she is foreign.
I think that life is nothing more than a dream.
I predict that we will have to open the green door to escape from this facility.
I gather from his words that his relationship with his wife is not currently at its best.
example_zh: 我发誓，那不是我干的。

name: 게
meaning: Expresses the purpose, method or though about the action that follows. It turns descriptive verb into adverb.
ko: 형용사를 부사로 바꾸거나 뒤 동작의 목적·방법을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: I went to school late today.
I cut my hair short.
Open your mouth wide and say "ah."
example_zh: 今天上学去晚了。

name: 게
meaning: Expect a result, criterion or standard in the following action and is necessary for the first clause to be realized.
examples: 사람들이 모두 보게 안내문 벽에 붙였다.
ko: 뒤 동작의 결과나 기준을 기대하며 앞 절의 실현을 이끄는 표현.
example_en: Come quickly so that we can eat dinner together.
They put up a notice on the wall so that everyone could see it.
example_zh: 为了一起吃晚饭，请快点来。

name: 게
meaning: Used to give commands or requests to a junior or someone with whom one is on familiar terms, in the 하게체 speech level.
ko: 하게체로 아랫사람에게 명령하거나 부탁하는 종결 어미.
example_en: Take a look at this.
Is that Mr. Kim? Come on in.
example_zh: 你看看这个。

name: 게끔
meaning: A result, criterion or standard in the following action is expected and necessary for the first clause to be realized. Like -게, but with more emphasis.
examples: 아무도 눈치를 채지 못하게끔 조심스럽게 과자를 훔쳐먹었다.
'떡밥'이란 알려지지 않았던 사실이나 반전 등을 작품에서 직접적으로 드러내기 전 그 사실을 조금이나마 유추할 수 있게끔 미리 작품속에 숨겨놓은 내용을 비유적으로 이르는 말이다.
ko: 앞 내용이 뒤 동작의 목표나 기준이 됨을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: I ate the snacks stealthily such that no one would notice.
'떡밥' is a figurative expression for the phenomenon in which a plot twist or new information is hinted at before it is directly revealed, so that readers have the chance to guess.
example_zh: 为了不让任何人察觉，我小心翼翼地偷吃了零食。

name: 게나
meaning: Used to give commands or requests to a junior or someone with whom one is on familiar terms, in the 하게체 speech level. Identical to :grammar[verb_게]{하게체-command} in meaning, but expresses a more familiar and friendly tone.
ko: 친한 사이나 아랫사람에게 권할 때 쓰는 하게체 종결 어미.
example_en: Come on in.
Let this be a secret between us.
Could you bring me a towel?
example_zh: 快进来吧。

name: 겠
meaning: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan to do something in the future.
ko: 앞으로 무엇을 하겠다는 말하는 사람의 의지를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I will start the treatment.
I will have to wait until it cools down a bit.
example_zh: 我这就开始操作。

name: 겠
meaning: Expresses the speaker's supposition about a certain situation.
ko: 어떤 상황에 대한 추측을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: This food looks really delicious!
This movie looks really fun!
example_zh: 这食物一定很好吃！

name: 겠거니
meaning: Expresses an assumption or supposition of the speaker about a particular situation.
examples: 다른 조원들이 지정된 일을 하겠거니 하고 컴퓨터 껐는데 다음 날에 등교했더니 아무것도 안 했더라고요.
첫번째 책이 좋아서 두번째 책도 좋겠거니 하고 샀는데, 읽어보니까 별로더라고요.
과민한 탓이겠거니 했는데 다시 생각해보니까 진짜 미행이 맞았던 것 같아요.
ko: 대략 그리 될 것이라고 짐작함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I figured my other project members would do their assigned work and turned my computer off, but when I came to school the next day I found they hadn't done anything.
Since the first book was good, I bought the second book thinking it would definitely be great, but turns out it was mid.
I thought I was just being overly sensitive, but thinking back on it, I think there really was someone following me.
example_zh: 我以为其他组员会做分配好的工作就把电脑关了，结果第二天到学校发现他们什么都没做。

name: 고
meaning: Used when listing two or more equals elements or facts.
examples: 제 남자 친구는 키가 크고 조금 통통한 편이에요.
ko: 여러 사실을 나란히 이어 주는 연결 어미.
example_en: The meeting was very pleasant and nice.
My boyfriend is tall and a bit chubby.
example_zh: 那次聚会非常愉快、美好。

name: 고
meaning: Used when the preceding and following statement happens in a sequential manner.
examples: 우리 아침도 안 먹고 나왔는데 국수나 먹고 갈까?
ko: 여러 사실을 나란히 이어 주는 연결 어미.
example_en: I met my friend and watched a movie.
We didn't even eat breakfast and came out. Should we eat noodles?
example_zh: 我见了朋友，然后看了电影。

name: 고말고
meaning: Emphasizes a positive response to a question from the other party.
ko: 물론 그러함을 강조하며 대답할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: That’s certainly good news.
Of course I'm all for it.
example_zh: 当然是件高兴的事。

name: 고서
meaning: When the first action get completed before the subsequent action started and there is a relationship between the two actions.
examples: 그 남자는 결혼을 하고서 사람이 달라졌어.
ko: 앞 동작이 끝난 뒤에 뒤 동작이 이어짐을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: Let's break through that door and rush into the palace!
He has changed after getting married.
example_zh: 让我们冲破那扇门，冲进宫殿吧！

name: 고자
meaning: State the intention or purpose for doing the action stated in the next clause. Used in formal situation.
examples: 저는 오늘 시민 여러분들의 의견을 듣고자 이 자리에 섰습니다.
한국어 실력을 늘리고자 한국 드라마를 자주 보고 있어요.
ko: 뒤 내용의 목적을 나타내는 격식 있는 연결 어미.
example_en: I am here to listen to the opinions of the citizens today.
I often watch Korean dramas to improve my Korean language skills.
example_zh: 我今天站在这里，是想聆听市民们的意见。

name: 고프다
meaning: Used to express a desire or wish to do something. A shortened form of :grammar[고_싶다].
ko: '-고 싶다'의 준말로, ~하고 싶은 마음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I want to dance too!
I finally saw the person I've wanted to see for a long time.
example_zh: 我也想跳舞！

name: 군(요)/구나/구먼
meaning: Express surprise after learning something new.
examples: 한 달 배운 것치고는 운전을 꽤 잘하는구나.
ko: 새로 알게 된 사실에 놀람을 나타내는 종결 어미.
example_en: You're quite good at driving for only having learned for a month.
All the side dishes at this restaurant are delicious.
That actor is really good at acting.
I misjudged your character!
example_zh: 才学了一个月，车开得挺好的嘛。

name: 그려
meaning: Emphasizes the contents of the sentence.
examples: 일주일 전에 나갔던 놈이 이제야 돌아왔네그려.
ko: 말하는 내용을 강조하는 감탄 조사(옛말투).
example_en: Let's meet up more often from now on.
That family's situation is really pitiful.
The guy who left a week ago has finally come back.
example_zh: 以后我们常常见面吧。

name: 기
meaning: Convert the preceding word as a noun.
ko: 앞말을 명사로 바꾸어 주는 접미사.
example_en: The pill is small, so it's easy to take.
It's hard to study while working.
example_zh: 那个药很小，容易服用。

name: 기는(요)
meaning: Expression is used to politely refute or disagree with the other person's statement. Used in response to a compliment to show modesty. Can also be used lightly criticize or scold someone.
ko: 상대의 말을 정중하게 부정하거나 겸손하게 대답하는 표현.
example_en: I'm not that good. There are many people who are better than me.
example_zh: 哪里做得好呀，比我做得好的人多着呢。

name: 기는(요)
meaning: In the form 기는/긴 하다, the speaker acknowledges that something is true or is indeed the case. It is often followed by -지만 or -는데/ㄴ데 grammar to form a partial acknowledgment with an objection.
examples: 니 말대로 이 라면이 맛이 좀 없긴 하네.
우리 아이가 시끄럽게 하기는 해도 말썽을 부리지는 않아. 그러니까 걱정하지 마.
한국어를 5년 전부터 공부해왔어요. 아직까진 잘 못하긴 하지만요.
ko: 어떤 사실을 인정하면서도 뒤에 이의를 붙이는 표현.
example_en: Like you said, this ramen really is kind of bad.
Even though my child can be noisy, they don't cause trouble. So don't worry.
I've studied Korean for 5 years. Although I must admit I'm still not very good.
example_zh: 如你所说，这泡面确实不太好吃。

name: 기에
meaning: Used to express the reason or cause for the speaker's action. Note that '-길래' is the conversational, spoken version of -기에.
examples: 사람들이 너무 많기에 다른 곳에 갔다.
ko: 말하는 사람의 행동에 대한 이유나 원인을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: Since the weather was warm, I went for a walk.
Because there were too many people, I went to a different place.
example_zh: 因为天气暖和，就去散步了。

name: 기에
meaning: The preceding clause expresses an often hypothetical situation, and the subsequent clause expresses a judgment related to the situation. Depending on whether the judgment is positive or negative, conditions for the situation can be either great or lacking. Often used with 는.
ko: 앞 절의 상황을 전제로 뒤 절에서 그에 대한 판단을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: The weather is just right for going to the beach.
I'm too full to eat cake.
We don't have enough people to play that game. It's for 8 or more players.
example_zh: 这天气正适合去海边。

name: 기에
meaning: Used with verbs like 보다, 느끼다, and 생각하다 at the start of a sentence to express one's point of view, or to ask another's point of view. Often used with 는.
examples: 제가 보기에는 아주 능력 있는 분이에요.
제가 느끼기에는 그 책은 초등학생이 읽기에는 적절하지 않아요.
ko: 보다·느끼다·생각하다와 함께 쓰여 자신의 관점을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: What do you think about it?
I think she's very capable.
I feel that that book is not appropriate for elementary schoolers to read.
example_zh: 在你看来怎么样？

name: 길래
meaning: Used to express the reason or cause for the speaker's action.
examples: 사람들이 너무 많길래 다른 곳에 갔어요.
ko: 화자 행동의 이유를 나타내는 구어적 연결 어미.
example_en: Since the weather was warm, I went for a walk.
Because there were too many people, I went to a different place.
example_zh: 天气暖和，所以就出去散步了。

name: 나니
meaning: Used by the speaker to provide some background information to the listener before connecting other related facts. It has a serious or solemn tone.
examples: 다시 묻나니 너는 어디에서 와서 어디로 가느냐.
ko: 앞 내용을 근거로 제시하며 뒤 내용을 이어 주는 연결 어미.
example_en: I trust you, so don’t let me down.
I ask you again: Where have you come from, and where are you going?
example_zh: 我相信你，别让我失望。

name: 나니
meaning: Expresses the first clause is the reason, condition, or basis for the second clause and should only be used with action verbs. It has a serious or solemn tone.
examples: 모든 준비가 끝났나니 이제 시작하도록 하자.
ko: 앞 내용을 근거로 제시하며 뒤 내용을 이어 주는 연결 어미.
example_en: Since you're sincerely apologizing, I will forgive you.
Now that everything is ready, let’s get started.
example_zh: 既然你真心道歉，我就原谅你。

name: 나이까
meaning: Used to ask a question in the 하소서체 speech level.
ko: 하소서체에서 아주 높이 질문할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: How could I possibly dare to disobey the royal command?
Master, did you call me?
How could I possibly say such a thing?
example_zh: 我怎敢违抗王命呢？

name: 나이다
meaning: Expresses a simple statement in 하소서체.
examples: 나라를 위하여 죽는 것이 제 영광이옵나이다.
ko: 하소서체로 간단히 진술할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: It is my honor to die for my country.
We pray to the Divine Spirit.
I shall proceed as ordered.
example_zh: 为国捐躯是我的荣光。

name: 냐
meaning: A casual interrogative ending in Korean, often used in informal speech to ask questions.
ko: 친한 사이에서 질문할 때 쓰는 반말 의문 어미.
example_en: How about trying a consultation once?
It's only the second day, and you're already fighting?
example_zh: 去咨询一次怎么样？

name: (으/느/이)냐고
meaning: It is used when the speaker quotes another person's question indirectly.
examples: 저는 몇 살이냐고 물어보는 게 제일 싫어요.
ko: 남의 질문을 간접적으로 인용할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: They asked me where I was going.
I hate it the most when people ask me how old I am.
They asked what my phone number was.
example_zh: 他问我要去哪儿。

name: 네(요)
meaning: Indicate that the speaker is impressed by a fact or situation they just learned about.
ko: 방금 알게 된 사실에 감탄함을 나타내는 종결 어미.
example_en: It's just like a scene from a drama.
You didn't turn on the TV today?
It's a relief that you found your wallet.
example_zh: 简直像电视剧里的一幕啊。

name: 노라
meaning: An archaic conjugation to informally express a simple statement or indirect quotation.
examples: 우리는 어떠한 어려움에 부닥쳐도 명예를 지키겠노라 맹세하였다.
ko: 간단한 진술이나 간접 인용을 나타내는 옛말 연결 어미.
example_en: I have returned victorious.
He said he had returned victorious.
We swore that we would uphold our honor no matter what difficulties we faced.
We write these words to bid farewell to our brother.
example_zh: （我）凯旋归来。

name: 노라면/느라면
meaning: Expresses a result that can happen when an action is done consistently.
examples: 홈쇼핑을 보고 있노라면 언제 시간이 갔는지 알 수 없을 지경이었다.
어머니 사진을 보느라면, 어머니가 보고 싶어져요.
ko: 어떤 일을 계속하는 상황에서 그런 결과가 생김을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: If you work hard, good days will come.
When I was watching home shopping channels, I couldn't tell when time passed.
Whenever I look at my mother's photo, I miss her.
example_zh: 努力生活的话，总会有好日子的。

name: 느니
meaning: Indicates that although neither of the two choices mentioned in the preceding and following clauses is ideal, the one in the following clause is the better option.
examples: 비가 오는 날에 걷느니 차라리 집에 있을래요.
혼자서 공부하느니 도서관에서 친구들과 같이 공부할게요.
ko: 둘 다 좋지 않지만 뒤의 것이 더 나음을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: Rather than walking on a rainy day, I'd rather stay at home.
Rather than studying alone, I'll study with friends at the library.
example_zh: 下雨天与其走路，我宁愿待在家里。

name: 느니
meaning: A connective ending used when listing words, thoughts, opinions, etc, that are usually opposite of one another.
examples: 그 두 사람 정말 결혼 할 수 있을까요? 결혼을 하느니 마느니 정말 말이 많던데요?
화초 색상이 안 어울린다느니, 키가 안 맞는다느니, 나불나불 말만 하던 김 대리는 갑자기 집에 일이 생겼다며 먼저 돌아갔다.
ko: 서로 반대되는 말이나 생각을 나열할 때 쓰는 연결 어미.
example_en: Can those two really get married? There's been so much talk about whether they should or shouldn't get married.
Assistant manager Kim, who had been chattering away about how the flower colors didn't match or how the height wasn't right, suddenly claimed he had something come up at home and left early.
example_zh: 那两个人真的能结婚吗？说要结也罢、不结也罢，大家议论得很多呢。

name: 느라(고)
meaning: Used when the action of the preceding statement is the purpose or cause of the following statement. Mostly used in negative scenario.
ko: 어떤 일에 몰두한 탓에 다른 결과가 생김을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: I couldn't answer the phone because I was taking a shower.
I spent all my money buying clothes.
It's hard to wake up in the morning to go to school.
example_zh: 因为洗澡，没能接电话。

name: 는고/(으)ㄴ고
meaning: It can be used to ask a question in a polite and gentle way.
ko: 정중하고 부드럽게 질문할 때 쓰는 옛 표현.
example_en: What would be a good gift?
Whose is this?
What are you hoping for?
example_zh: 什么礼物好呢？

name: 는고/(으)ㄴ고
meaning: Expresses the speaker's speculation, curiosity or assumption about something.
examples: 일이 해결이 되다니 이 얼마나 좋은고?
ko: 정중하고 부드럽게 질문할 때 쓰는 옛 표현.
example_en: What a wonderful thing!
Isn't it wonderful that the problem has been solved?
Why did I say that?
What have I done wrong?
example_zh: 这是多么了不起的事啊！

name: (는)구려/(는)구료
meaning: Express surprise after learning something new.
ko: 하오체로 새로운 사실을 알게 된 놀라움을 나타내는 종결 어미.
example_en: Wow, this is a really clean neighborhood.
You must have been really disappointed to hear that.
You’re really eating well today.
example_zh: 这街区真干净啊。

name: (는)구려/(는)구료
meaning: Expresses a command in a polite, suggestive tone.
examples: 더 늦으면 어두워질 테니 어서 가구려.
ko: 하오체로 정중하게 권하듯 명령하는 종결 어미.
example_en: It'll get dark soon so let's get going.
Why don't you offer this person a drink, too?
example_zh: 再晚天就要黑了，快走吧。

name: (ㄴ/는)다기보다는/(이)라기보다는
meaning: This phrase is used to show that the information in the next part of the sentence describes the topic better than the information in the previous part.
examples: 이 장소가 시끄럽다기보다는 사람들이 많이 모여서 복잡해요.
그 가수가 유명하다기보다는 독특한 목소리로 알려져 있어요.
ko: 앞의 표현보다 뒤의 표현이 더 정확함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Rather than saying this place is noisy, it's more accurate to say it is crowded because many people gather here.
Rather than saying the singer is famous, it's more accurate to say they are known for their unique voice.
example_zh: 与其说这地方吵，不如说人聚得多、很拥挤。

name: (ㄴ/는)다는, (이)라는
meaning: Used to quote other people or yourself.
examples: 이 분수에 동전을 던지면 행복해진다는 이야기가 있어요.
ko: 남의 말이나 자신의 말을 인용하여 꾸밀 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: There is a story that you will be happy if you throw a coin into this fountain.
Did you hear that 주연 is getting married?
example_zh: 有个传说，往这个喷泉里扔硬币就会变得幸福。

name: (ㄴ/는)다면
meaning: Used to express a hypothetical situation contrary to what actually happened in the past or now or situation that have yet to occurs.
examples: 10년 전 돌아간다면 더 열심히 공부하고 싶어.
날씨가 좋았다면 한라산에 갈 수 있었을 텐데.
지난 학기에 열심히 공부하지 않았다면 장학금을 받을 수 없었겠지?
ko: 실제와 반대되는 일이나 가정을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: If I could go back 10 years, I would want to study harder.
If the weather had been good, I could have gone to 한라산.
If you hadn't studied hard last semester, you wouldn't have been able to get a scholarship, right?
example_zh: 如果能回到10年前，我想更努力学习。

name: (ㄴ/는)답시고
meaning: Expresses that someone attempts to do something, but ends up causing a bad result.
examples: 아기가 엄마를 도와준답시고 설거지를 하다가 주방을 엉망으로 만들었다.
친구가 공부한답시고 도서관에 갔지만 잠만 잤다.
그녀가 웃긴 이야기 한답시고 했는데 아무도 안 웃었다.
ko: ~라고 내세웠는데 결과가 좋지 않음을 비꼬는 표현.
example_en: My brother tried to fix the phone but ended up breaking it.
The baby tried to help mom with the dishes but made a mess in the kitchen.
My friend claimed to study at the library but just slept.
She tried to tell a funny story but no one laughed.
example_zh: 弟弟说要修手机，结果摆弄一通反而把它弄坏了。

name: 는지라/(으)ㄴ지라
meaning: Indicates that the first clause is the reason or cause for the second clause.
examples: 선생님께서 고집을 굽히지 않으시는지라 우리도 어쩔 수 없었다.
이미 밥을 먹은지라 더 이상 먹을 수가 없다.
나는 어릴 적부터의 친구인지라 그의 마음을 잘 안다.
기분이 좋은지라 다른 사람에게도 다정하게 말을 건다.
ko: 앞 내용이 뒤 내용의 이유가 됨을 나타내는 문어체 어미.
example_en: Since the teacher won't budge, there was nothing we could do.
I already ate, so I can’t eat any more.
Since we've been friends since childhood, I know exactly how he feels.
Since I'm in a good mood, I speak kindly to others as well.
example_zh: 老师不肯让步，我们也没有办法。

name: (ㄴ/는)다
meaning: A sentence final ending used to describe an event or fact of the present.
ko: 현재의 사실이나 일반적인 진술을 나타내는 종결 어미.
example_en: The wind is cool.
My family lives in an apartment.
example_zh: 风很凉快。

name: 다가
meaning: Expresses the speaker's interruption of one action to immediately start another action.
examples: 누워서 영상을 보다가 핸드폰을 손에서 놓쳤어요.
ko: 어떤 동작을 하다가 멈추고 다른 동작으로 옮겨감을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: I was eating when I received a phone call.
I was lying down watching a video when I dropped my phone.
example_zh: 我正吃着饭接了个电话。

name: 다가
meaning: It can also be used to express that the action in the first clause continues while the action in the second clause occurs.
ko: 어떤 동작을 하다가 멈추고 다른 동작으로 옮겨감을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: I was sleeping and had a scary dream.
I was on my way home when I met a friend.
example_zh: 睡觉时做了个噩梦。

name: 다가는
meaning: Used to express the speaker's view that if the action in the first clause happens then a negative result might occur in the future
examples: 돈을 계획 없이 쓰다가는 필요할 때 돈이 부족할지도 몰라요.
ko: 그렇게 하다 보면 좋지 않은 결과가 생김을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: You'll be in big trouble if you make a mistake.
You might run out of money when you need it if you spend it without a plan.
example_zh: 一旦失手就会出大事。

name: (ㄴ/는)다거나, (이)라거나
meaning: Used to indirectly reference something when listing options.
examples: 다솜은 친구랑 통화한다거나 좋아하는 웹툰을 정주행한다거나 하는 것으로 스트레스를 푼다.
수민이가 자꾸 나한테 장난을 치거나 바보라거나 해서 진짜 못 참겠다.
그 돌을 신으로 모신다거나 뭐 그런 거였습니까?
감각이 둔하다거나 마수 사냥 경험이 부족하다면 충분히 혼란스러울 수 있는 상황이었지만 유노는 어느 쪽에도 해당하지 않았다.
ko: 여러 선택지를 나열하며 간접적으로 언급할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Dasom relieves stress by doing things like calling a friend or binging a favorite webtoon.
Sumin keeps playing jokes on me or calling me stupid and I really can't stand it.
Were they worshipping that stone as a god or something?
It could have been a disorienting situation for someone with dull senses or lacking in monster hunting experience, but neither was true for Yuno.
example_zh: 多松靠和朋友通电话，或者追喜欢的网漫之类的来解压。

name: (는/ㄴ)다고
meaning: Used to pass along what the speaker heard from another person, or to present the subject's thoughts, opinions, etc.
examples: 비가 온다고요? 스키 타러 가려고 했는데 못 가겠네요.
회의가 조금 있으면 끝난다고 하니까 끝나자마자 빨리 갈게요.
ko: 들은 말이나 남의 생각·의견을 전할 때 쓰는 인용 표현.
example_en: I heard that you're going to Korea tomorrow.
Is it going to rain? I was going to go skiing but I can't go now.
They said the meeting will end soon, so I'll leave as soon as it's over.
example_zh: 我听说你明天要去韩国。

name: 다니/라니/냐니/자니
meaning: Expression to show the speaker's reaction, shock or disbelief to something they just learned, heard, saw or experienced.
examples: 두 달 동안 살을 10kg이나 빼다니 정말이에요?
친구에게 내일 등산을 가겠냐니 싫다고 하더라.
그래 너희 남편은 이번 여름에 어디로 휴가를 가자니?
ko: 방금 알게 된 일에 놀라거나 믿기지 않을 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: You lost 10kg in two months, really?
What did that person say to you?
My friend said they don't want to go hiking tomorrow.
So where is your husband planning to go on vacation this summer?
example_zh: 两个月瘦了10公斤，真的吗？

name: (ㄴ/는)다니까/(이)라니까
meaning: Reminds the listener about something already said, or about a prediction that came true.
examples: 이게 정답이라니까, 더 이상 의심하지 마.
ko: 이미 말한 것을 다시 강조할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: I told you I canceled the appointment, why did you wait?
I told you I’m going home, don't worry.
Since this is the correct answer, don't doubt it any further.
example_zh: 我都说了预约取消了，你还等什么？

name: (ㄴ)다든가, (이)라든가
meaning: -라든가 is used to list various descriptions that can be selected. (ㄴ)다든가 follows verbs or adjectives to list various propositions that can be selected. These descriptions or propositions are mainly theoretical, which is the distinction between this grammar and -든가.
examples: 집에 누군가 찾아오지는 않았습니까? 아니면 전화가 걸려왔다든가...
요즘 미나에게 고민거리 같은 건 없었니? 성적이라든가, 가족 문제라든가. 남자친구와 싸웠다든가 하는 거 말이야.
이 답장을 보내기 위해 저는 말도 안 되는 계획을 실행할 예정이고, 그 결과로 유치장에 갇힌다든가 연구원직을 박탈당한다든가 하는 상당한 징계를 받게 되겠죠.
그 여자 좀 별로였거든. 얼굴이 이상했다든가 성격이 괴팍했다든가 그런 건 아닌데, 느낌이 영 별로야.
ko: 여러 가지를 나열하며 선택의 여지를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Did no one come by the house? Or make a call or something...
Was Mina worried about anything recently? Like grades, family problems, or something like fighting with her boyfriend.
I plan to enact a ridiculous plan to send this response, and I'm sure I'll face a sizable punishment, whether it be being thrown in jail or having my research position revoked.
I don't like her. It's not like her face looked strange or her personality was weird, but the vibes are just not good.
example_zh: 没有人来过家里吗？还是说打来过电话什么的……

name: (ㄴ)다든지, (이)라든지
meaning: An abbreviation of '-다고/라고 하든지' used to suggest that any of the stated descriptions are possible.
examples: 유학 생활이 힘들다든지 한국어 공부가 어렵다든지 하며 불평만 하지 마세요.
실종이 물론 우연은 아니겠죠. 어떤 사고에 휘말렸다든지...
뭐라도 지금 좀 갖다 줘. 간단한 빵이라든지, 수프라든지.
ko: 어느 쪽이든 가능함을 나타내는 나열 표현.
example_en: Don't just complain about studying abroad being tough or Korean learning being difficult.
His disappearance cannot be a coincidence. He may have gotten involved in an accident...
Just bring me something, anything. Like some simple bread or soup.
example_zh: 别光抱怨留学生活辛苦、韩语学习难什么的。

name: 다마다
meaning: Emphasizes a positive response to a question from the other party.
examples: 도와달라 말했는가. 물론일세! 좋다마다! 얼마든지 도와줌세!
ko: 물론 그러함을 강조하며 대답할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Yeah, you’re right.
You asked for help? Of course! That's great! I’ll help you as much as I can!
example_zh: 嗯，你说得对。

name: 다면서(요)
meaning: Used to confirm with another person something that the speaker heard previously from some other source.
examples: 한국 사람들이 거의 날마다 김치를 먹는다면서요?
방학 동안 스웨덴에 갔었다면서? 춥지 않았어?
ko: 다른 데서 들은 내용을 상대에게 확인할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: I heard that Korean people eat kimchi almost every day, is it true?
I heard you went to Sweden during the vacation? Wasn't it cold?
I heard you've already finished everything?
example_zh: 听说韩国人几乎天天吃泡菜，是真的吗？

name: 다시피
meaning: Used to express the confirmation of a fact that the listener is already aware of.
ko: 상대도 아는 사실을 확인하듯 나타내는 표현.
example_en: As you can see, the weather is nice.
As you can hear, the music is very good.
example_zh: 如你所见，天气很好。

name: 더
meaning: Express and convey in the present a fact directly experienced or witnessed in the past.
examples: 어제 그 식당 음식이 참 맛있더군요.
ko: 과거에 직접 보거나 경험한 일을 지금 회상하여 나타내는 선어말 어미.
example_en: As I remember, everyone was excited that day.
I experienced that the food at that restaurant yesterday was really delicious.
I saw that the children were playing happily at the playground.
I noticed Minji played the piano really well.
From my experience, that movie was more boring than I expected.
I recall the exhibition I visited last week being very interesting.
example_zh: 记得那天大家都兴奋得很。

name: 더냐
meaning: Used to ask about what the listener personally saw or heard in the past.
ko: 상대가 과거에 직접 본 일을 물을 때 쓰는 옛 표현.
example_en: Was it snowing when you arrived in Japan?
Who told you do say that?
example_zh: 你到日本的时候下雪了吗？

name: 더니
meaning: Used when the speaker wants to refer to a change compared to the past that they have directly seen or experienced. The speaker themself cannot be the subject.
examples: 아침에는 하늘에 구름 한 점 없는 게 하루 종일 맑을 것 같더니, 금방 비가 쏟아지네.
어릴 때 편식을 하더니 이제 나도 못 먹는 것까지 잘 먹는구나.
ko: 과거와 비교하여 달라진 변화를 직접 겪은 대로 나타내는 어미.
example_en: In the morning, there wasn't a single cloud in the sky, so it looked like it would be clear all day, but not long after it started to pour.
You were so picky when you were little, but now you even eat things that I don't eat.
example_zh: 早上天上一点云都没有，看样子一整天都会晴，可很快就下起了大雨。

name: 더니
meaning: Used to narrate a sequence of events directly observed by the speaker. The subjects of both clauses are usually but not always the same, and the speaker cannot be the subject. There is often a nuance that the first clause becomes the cause of the second clause.
examples: 미나는 부엌에 가더니 5분 만에 라면을 만들어 냈다.
이야기 중이던 맥스가 우리의 대화를 가만히 듣고 서 있는 앨리스를 흘긋 쳐다보더니 입을 닫았다.
눈시울이 점점 붉어지더니 제이콥이 결국 참지 못하고 펑펑 울기 시작했다.
ko: 직접 관찰한 일이 순서대로 이어짐을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: Mina went to the kitchen and made ramen in just 5 minutes.
It was cloudy and then it snowed.
Max, who had been telling a story, glanced at Alice, who was listening quietly to our conversation, and then closed his mouth.
Jacob's eyes grew red until he couldn't hold it in anymore and started to sob.
example_zh: 美娜进了厨房，5分钟就做出了拉面。

name: 더니
meaning: Used to express the existence of an additional event or truth related to something in the past.
examples: 요즘 부동산에 집 보러 다니더니 좋은 집을 찾았어요?
ko: 과거의 일과 관련된 또 다른 사실을 덧붙이는 어미.
example_en: You've been looking at houses lately. Did you find a good one?
example_zh: 你最近在看房子，找到好的了吗？

name: 더라고(요)
meaning: Used to relate something that the speaker came to know through direct past experience. Usually conjugated in present tense. Often used as '-더라' in casual speech.
examples: 이 제품이 요즘 청소년들에게 정말 인기가 많더라고요.
한국에 처음 왔을 때 외국인이 별로 없더라고요.
ko: 과거의 직접 경험을 전할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: When I arrived in Japan, it was snowing.
This product is really popular among young people these days.
Minjoo is seriously good at soccer.
There weren't many foreigners in Korea when I first came.
example_zh: 我到日本的时候，正下着雪呢。

name: 더라고(요)
meaning: Used in casual speech to wonder to oneself while recalling a past event, or to ask the listener about a shared past experience. 뭐더라 / 뭐였더라 can be filler words.
ko: 과거의 직접 경험을 전할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: When did we first meet again?
What's that singer's name again?
Hmm, where did I go yesterday?
example_zh: 我们第一次见面是在什么时候来着？

name: 더라도
meaning: Indicates that the second clause will happens regardless of the described state or action of the first clause. Stronger in meaning than 아/어도. Often used to speculate or theorize.
examples: 식당에 일찍 가서 줄 서 있더라도 웨이팅이 오래 걸릴 수도 있어요.
라면은 매일 먹더라도 질리지 않을 것 같아요.
헤어진 상대를 훨씬 더 멋있는 모습으로 마주치게 되면 상대방을 후회하게 만들 수 있고, 후회까지는 아니더라도 조금의 씁쓸함을 안겨줄 수 있습니다.
ko: 앞 내용과 상관없이 뒤 내용이 그러함을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: Even if we go to the restaurant early and stand in line, it might take a while to get in.
I don't think I'll get tired of eating ramen even if I eat it every day.
If you run into an ex and you're looking much better than before, you can make them regret the breakup, or even if it doesn't go as far as regret, you can make them feel a little bitter.
example_zh: 就算早早去餐厅排队，也可能要等很久。

name: 더라면
meaning: Used to hypothesize a past situation that is the opposite of what actually happened, usually to express the speaker's regret or disappointment or the relief of not doing it.
examples: 제가 키가 컸더라면 모델이 되었을 거예요.
제가 2분 빨리 집을 나갔더라면 버스를 안 놓쳤을 거에요.
돈을 아껴서 썼더라면 다른 사람에게 돈을 빌리지 않아도 됐을 텐데.
ko: 과거와 반대되는 상황을 가정할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: If I had been taller, I would have become a model.
If I had left home 2 minutes earlier, I wouldn't have missed the bus.
If I had saved money, I wouldn't have had to borrow money from others.
example_zh: 我要是个子高一点，就当上模特了。

name: 던
meaning: Used to share or ask about a past experience. The past experience must have been habitual and not a one-time occurrence.
examples: 어릴 때 엄마가 해주시던 밥이 정말 맛있었어.
신입 사원일 때 자주 입던 옷인데 지금도 가끔 입어.
ko: 과거에 반복되던 습관적인 일을 나타내는 관형사형 어미.
example_en: The food my mom would make for me when I was little was really delicious.
I wore this outfit a lot when I was new to the company, and I still wear it occasionally now.
example_zh: 小时候妈妈常做给我的饭真的很好吃。

name: 던
examples: 전화가 울렸을 때 읽던 책을 접고 받았다.
ko: 과거에 하다 만 동작을 나타내는 관형사형 어미.
example_en: My little brother stole and ate the ramen I had been eating.
Go back to what you had been doing.
When the phone rang, I closed the book I had been reading and picked up the call.
example_zh: 我吃到一半的拉面被弟弟偷吃了。

name: 던
meaning: Implies that an event or action might have not been completed in the past and has been stopped since.
examples: '김'이라는 성은 신라에 살고 있던 귀족들의 성씨였어요.
ko: 과거의 동작이 완결되지 않았음을 함축하는 관형사형 어미.
example_en: The surname '김' was the surname of the nobles who lived in Silla.
example_zh: 「金」这个姓是新罗时期贵族的姓氏。

name: 던가
meaning: Used exclusively in 하게체 to ask the listener about a past event. 하게체 is a register of speech that slightly lowers the listener and is falling out of fashion as of recently. It sounds extremely awkward when used by younger people.
ko: 과거의 일을 물을 때 쓰는 하게체 표현.
example_en: Was that restaurant good?
What did she say?
example_zh: 那家餐厅好吃吗？

name: 던가
meaning: Used to wonder to oneself about something in the past or to make a guess about a past event.
examples: 혹시 내가 기분을 안 좋게 했던가 해서 걱정했지.
ko: 과거의 일을 물을 때 쓰는 하게체 표현.
example_en: Did I say that?
Were they really that close?
I was worried that maybe I had hurt your feelings.
example_zh: 我那么说过吗？

name: 던데(요)
meaning: Used to express surprise or disbelief toward a past event or particular situation based on something that the speaker saw or experienced. Expecting an answer from the listener. Can also be used to make a contradiction.
examples: 제가 오늘 학교에 왔을 때 교실에 아무도 없던데요.
ko: 과거에 경험한 일을 근거로 느낌을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: (I saw that) That person was quite good at soccer.
When I came to school today, (I saw that) there was no one in the classroom.
There were many delicious foods there.
example_zh: 那人足球踢得还挺不错的呢。

name: 던데(요)
meaning: Similar to ㄴ/는데, but with the added nuance that the speaker has seen or experienced the fact or situation described in that clause. When a '다' is added in front (-다던데), it is used to convey that the speaker has heard from someone that something is the case.
examples: 너 요즘 이상한 사람들이랑 어울리던데 괜찮아?
ko: 과거에 경험한 일을 근거로 느낌을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I've noticed you've been hanging out with some strange people recently. Are you okay?
I've heard / people say that Korean food is spicy -- is that true?
example_zh: 你最近总和一些奇怪的人混在一起，没事吧？

name: 데(요)
meaning: Used to relate something that the speaker came to know through direct past experience.
examples: 오늘 시험 공부를 열심히 했는데 끝나고 보니까 새벽 2시데요.
우리 할머니 고향은 하나도 안 변했데.
ko: 직접 경험한 사실을 이유나 상황으로 제시할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: Japanese people frequently eat takoyaki.
I studied hard for my exam today and when I was done, it turned out to be 2 in the morning.
My grandma's hometown hadn't changed at all.
example_zh: （听说）日本人经常吃章鱼烧。

name: 도다/로다
meaning: An archaic ending used to express admiration in a solemn tone.
examples: 평생을 조국을 위해 헌신하였으니 참으로 애국자도다.
독하도다. 독하도다. 서울 양반 독하도다. 원수로다. 원수로다. 존비귀천 원수로다.
ko: 장중하게 감탄을 나타내는 옛말 종결 어미.
example_en: Having devoted his entire life to his country, he is truly a patriot.
Well done, students.
How cruel! How cruel! How cruel are the Seoul aristocrats! They are my enemies. They are my enemies. High and low, they are all my enemies.
example_zh: 他一生为祖国奉献，真乃爱国志士啊。

name: 도록
meaning: It expresses that the preceding clause is the goal or reason for doing the action stated in the following clause.
examples: 아침에 일찍 일어나도록 어젯밤에 일찍 잤어요.
필요할 때 잘 찾아볼 수 있도록 정리를 잘 해 두세요.
음식은 상하지 않도록 냉장고에 넣어 두는 게 좋겠어요.
ko: 뒤 동작의 목표나 범위가 됨을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: I went to bed early last night so that I could wake up early in the morning.
Organize things well so that you can find them easily when you need them.
It would be better to put food in the refrigerator so that it doesn't spoil.
example_zh: 为了早上能早起，昨晚睡得很早。

name: 든가
meaning: Similar to 든지. Expresses that either one of the two stated actions or situations is acceptable. If there is only one stated action, it can be a suggestion that the listener do the stated action "or something" and is often motivated by anger or passive-aggression. Is sometimes written as "-던가" although this is not standard spelling.
examples: 아, 들으라고 한 소리는 아니구나? 그럼 말소리를 좀 작게 소곤대면서 하든가. 아니면 어디 구석에 찌그러져서 지껄이든가.
밥이 없으니 점심으로 라면을 끓이든가 빵을 먹든가 해.
가: 빨리 원하는 거나 사. 좀 이따 친구랑 약속 있는데... 빨리 끝내자. 나: 그럼 그냥 가든가!
ko: 둘 중 아무것나 괜찮음을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: Oh, [what you just said] wasn't meant to be heard? Then maybe you should whisper it. Or squish yourselves into a corner before prattling on.
There's no rice, so boil ramen or eat bread for lunch.
A: Just hurry up and buy whatever you want. I have plans with a friend in a bit... let's finish up quickly. B: Then just go!
example_zh: 哦，刚才那话不是要说给人听的？那你就小声嘀咕着说，要么就缩到哪个角落里去念叨。

name: 든지
meaning: Used when any of the stated choices are fine, express a contrast between the options. Require at least 2 options.
examples: 누구든지 언제든지 참여하실 수 있는 챌린지니까.
대학교에 진학하든지 진학하지 않든지 열심히 공부해야 돼요.
ko: 어느 쪽이든 상관없음을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: Anyone can participate whenever.
You have to study hard whether you go to college or not.
example_zh: 任何人任何时候都可以参加这个挑战。

name: 듯이
meaning: A connective ending used when the following statement is almost the same to the preceding statement.
ko: 앞 내용처럼 뒤 내용이 그러함을 비유하여 나타내는 어미.
example_en: Why are you drinking like you're fighting?
The singer spoke as if singing.
example_zh: 你怎么喝得像打架一样？

name: (이/으)라고
meaning: It can be used to quote what the speaker heard from another person. Indirectly quoting a declarative sentence. Used to ask for clarification or reconfirmation of something they just heard.
ko: 명령이나 요구를 간접적으로 인용할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: They said their family has four members.
What did the teacher say?
example_zh: 他们说家里一共有4口人。

name: (이/으)라고
meaning: It can also be used to quote an imperative statement. Can be an instruction or command.
examples: 일곱 시까지 돌아오라고 일렀거늘 왜 늦었느냐?
의사가 매운 음식을 먹지 말라고 했다.
ko: 명령이나 요구를 간접적으로 인용할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: I told you to come back by seven, why are you late?
The doctor said not to eat spicy food.
example_zh: 叫你7点前回来，怎么迟到了？

name: (으)려거든
meaning: Very similar to -(으)려면, but less common. Expresses that if the listener intends to take an action, then they should act according to the second clause (the part that comes after the (으)려거든)
examples: 건강한 치아를 유지하려거든 하루에 두번 이 닦아야 해요.
여러 나라의 요리를 배우려거든 요리학원에 등록해보세요.
ko: 그렇게 하고 싶다면,의 뜻으로 조건을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: If you want to maintain your dental health, you have to brush your teeth twice a day.
If you want to learn how to cook food from a lot of different countries, try enrolling in a cooking hakwon.
example_zh: 要想保持牙齿健康，每天得刷两次牙。

name: 로군(요)/로구나/로구먼/로고
meaning: Express surprise after learning something new. Only used with '이다' and '아니다' (sometimes in combination with '-으시'), and is stronger than 군(요)/구나/구먼 in these special cases. 로고 is an archaic form of the other three.
examples: 그건 그냥 마음이 변했기 때문... 아니, 그게 아니로군요.
길을 잘 모르는 걸 보니 이번이 초행길이시로구먼.
역겨운 아해들이로고! 옛날과 달라진 바가 하나도 없다!
ko: '이다/아니다'와 함께 새로 알게 된 사실에 놀람을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Ah, you're talking about that man. (That's who you're talking about)
I see -- so that's why you're not in a good mood.
That's simply because she changed her mind... no, wait, that's not it.
Seeing as you don't know the way, this must be your first time here.
You disgusting brats! Nothing has changed since the old days!
example_zh: 啊，你说的是那个男人啊。

name: 마는/만
meaning: Acknowledges a preceding fact while expressing doubts about it or situations that contradict it.
examples: 너도 가지마는 그다지 재미는 없을 것이다.
영화를 보고는 싶지마는 시간이 안 난다.
ko: 앞 내용을 인정하면서 뒤에 반대되는 내용을 이어 주는 표현.
example_en: It probably isn't much, but please use it to supplement your needs.
You can go too, but it probably won't be much fun.
I’d like to see a movie, but I don’t have the time.
I want to buy it but I don't have the money.
You said you were going to rest at home, so why did you come out?
example_zh: 虽然没多少，但拿去贴补着用吧。

name: (으)며
meaning: Indicates that two or more actions are happening at the same time.
examples: 빨갛고 매운 음식을 먹으며 스트레스를 푸는 장면을 본 적이 있나요?
ko: 두 가지 이상의 동작이 동시에 일어남을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: I study while singing.
Have you ever seen a scene where you de-stress by eating red and spicy food?
example_zh: 我一边唱歌一边学习。

name: (으)며
meaning: Used to list two or more actions, states, or facts. Mainly used in written language or formal situations.
examples: 그곳은 마치 고향처럼 아늑하고 포근하며 정겨운 느낌을 주는 곳이다.
한국 사람들은 매운 음식을 좋아하며 일을 빨리 처리한다고 들었다.
ko: 둘 이상의 동작·상태·사실을 나열하는 연결 어미.
example_en: That place is cozy, warm, and give a feeling like home.
I heard that Koreans like spicy food and get things done quickly.
example_zh: 那个地方像故乡一样安逸温馨，充满人情味。

name: (으)며
meaning: When used with 이다, it used to list two or more things or statement. Also implies that they are large in number and there are more than just the listed items.
examples: 무며 오이며 부추며 갖가지 채소로 김치를 담근다.
ko: 이다와 함께 쓰여 둘 이상의 것을 나열하는 표현.
example_en: I don't care about money or fame.
Kimchi is made from various vegetables such as white radishes, cucumbers, and leeks.
example_zh: 无论是钱还是名誉，我都不关心。

name: (으)면
meaning: Used when the preceding statement becomes the condition of the following statement.
examples: 공부를 열심히 하면 좋은 성적이 좋아집니다.
내일 시간이 있으면 같이 영화를 볼래요?
ko: 앞 내용이 뒤 내용의 조건이나 가정이 됨을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: If you study hard, your grades will improve.
Shall we watch a movie together if you have time tomorrow?
example_zh: 努力学习的话，成绩就会变好。

name: (으)면
meaning: Used to suppose or assume something that has not yet happened.
examples: 내가 죽으면 우리 아이들은 누가 돌보니?
ko: 앞 내용이 뒤 내용의 조건이나 가정이 됨을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: When I die, who will take care of our children?
When the exam is over, I will take a good rest.
example_zh: 我死后，谁来照顾我们的孩子？

name: (으)면
meaning: Used to indicate a habitual and repetitive condition.
examples: 남편은 내가 잠들어 있으면 깨우지 않으려고 살금살금 걸어 다닌다.
ko: 앞 내용이 뒤 내용의 조건이나 가정이 됨을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: My husband walks around quietly so as not to wake me up when I'm asleep.
example_zh: 我睡着的时候，丈夫为了不吵醒我会蹑手蹑脚地走动。

name: (으)면서
meaning: Indicates that two or more actions are happening at the same time.
ko: 두 동작이 동시에 일어남을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: We talked while eating.
I sang while dancing.
I am reading the news while waiting for my friend.
example_zh: 我们边吃饭边聊天。

name: (으)세요
meaning: A polite imperative form used to give instructions or make requests.
ko: 정중하게 지시하거나 부탁하는 명령형.
example_en: Please sit here.
Please go straight on this road.
Please be careful.
example_zh: 请坐这里。

name: (으)세요
meaning: Politely ask about someone's action or state.
ko: 상대의 동작이나 상태를 정중하게 묻는 표현.
example_en: Where are you now?
What do you do?
Do you have time?
What kind of music do you like?
example_zh: 您现在在哪儿？

name: (으)세요
meaning: Used to politely state someone's action or state.
ko: 상대의 동작이나 상태를 정중하게 서술하는 표현.
example_en: The teacher teaches Korean.
My parents are in Seoul.
It's your birthday.
My grandmother is ill.
example_zh: 老师教韩语。

name: (으)소서
meaning: Used to express a request or wish in an extremely polite fashion. Most often used when speaking to kings, queens, and God.
examples: 주님을 믿사오며 나의 마음에 용기를 채워주소서.
ko: 아주 정중하게 간청하거나 소망을 나타내는 옛 종결 어미.
example_en: O Lord, do not forsake us!
As I trust in you Lord, please fill my heart with courage.
Help me overcome the hardships of this diet.
Listen to what I have to say.
example_zh: 神啊，请不要抛弃我们！

name: (스)ㅂ니까
meaning: Used when the speaker asks the listener politely.
ko: 정중하게 질문할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: What time do you usually go to bed?
Could you lend me your husband for a moment?
Do you have any questions?
example_zh: 您通常几点睡？

name: (스)ㅂ니다
meaning: Used to explain the present action, state, or fact politely.
examples: 저를 살려 주신 은혜를 꼭 갚고 싶습니다.
ko: 정중하게 사실을 설명할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: Grandfather praised me.
I have never harmed anyone.
I want to repay the favor of saving me.
example_zh: 爷爷表扬了我。

name: (스)ㅂ니다만
meaning: Politely present contrasting information after stating a fact.
examples: 이 연구는 중요한 의미가 있습니다만 아직 한계점이 많이 존재합니다.
정부 발표 내용은 분명합니다만 일부 시민단체에서 반발하고 있습니다.
지금까지 훌륭한 결과를 내었습니다만 앞으로 더 많은 데이터가 필요할 것 같습니다.
작년 실적은 향상되었습니다만 여전히 예산 문제가 해결되지 않았습니다.
교수님의 이론은 타당합니다만 실제 적용 사례를 더 살펴볼 필요가 있을 것 같습니다.
ko: 정중하게 말한 뒤 반대되는 내용을 이어 주는 표현.
example_en: This research has significant meaning, but there are still many limitations.
The government's announcement is clear, however some civic groups are protesting against it.
We've achieved excellent results so far, but I believe we'll need more data moving forward.
Last year's performance improved, however the budget issue still remains unresolved.
Professor, your theory is valid, but I think we need to examine more real-world application cases.
example_zh: 这项研究意义重大，但目前还存在很多局限。

name: (으)시
meaning: Honor the subject of the sentence. Show respect to a person, their possessions or body part.
examples: 저도 곧 따라갈 테니까 먼저 출발하시지요.
ko: 문장의 주어를 높이는 존칭 선어말 어미.
example_en: Would you like to add more salt to the soup?
Would you like to sit here?
I will follow you soon, so please go ahead.
example_zh: 汤里要再加点盐吗？

name: 아/어/여
meaning: Describe a certain fact, ask a question, give an order, or advise.
ko: 사실을 말하거나 묻고 명령하는 등의 구어적 종결을 이루는 어미.
example_en: I go to school.
That girl is really pretty.
The weather is really nice.
Where does that person live?
example_zh: 我去上学。

name: 아/어다가
meaning: It expresses that the second clause is performed based on the result of first completing the action in the first clause. The first and seconds clause must happens in different locations.
examples: 저녁에 피자과 지킨을 시켜다가 집에서 먹을까요?
ko: 앞 동작의 결과를 가지고 뒤 동작을 함을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: I made a cake and gave it to my friend.
Shall we order pizza and chicken for dinner and eat at home?
I will go to the bank and get the money for you.
example_zh: 我做了个蛋糕，送给了朋友。

name: 아/어도
meaning: Indicates that the second clause will happens regardless of the described state or action of the first clause.
ko: 앞 내용에 상관없이 뒤 내용이 그러함을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: I don't study <f>even if</f> I buy books.
I don't get tired of eating ramen <f>even if</f> I eat it every day.
Are you going to travel <f>even if</f> it rains?
example_zh: 就算买了书我也不学习。

name: 아/어/여라
meaning: Used to give commands or requests in an informal manner.
examples: 창문을 닫아라. 바람이 너무 많이 들어와.
ko: 친한 사이나 아랫사람에게 명령할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: Eat your rice.
Go home and do your homework.
Close the window. Too much wind is coming in.
example_zh: 吃饭吧。

name: 아/어서
meaning: The first clause is the reason for or the cause of the second clause.
ko: 앞 내용이 뒤 내용의 이유나 근거가 됨을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: I can't wear these clothes because they're too small.
I can't meet my friends because I'm busy these days.
example_zh: 那件衣服太小，穿不了。

name: 아/어서
meaning: A connective ending to indicate a temporal relationship between events. The second clause can only happen after the first action has happened.
examples: 내일 친구를 만나서 영화를 볼 거예요.
조금 더 돈을 모아서 장난감을 살까요?
ko: 앞 내용이 뒤 내용의 이유나 근거가 됨을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: I'm going to meet my friend tomorrow in order to watch a movie.
Should we save a little more money in order to buy toys?
example_zh: 我明天打算见朋友，然后一起看电影。

name: 았/었/였
meaning: Indicate that an event happened in the past.
examples: 어제 배가 아팠어요. 그래서 잠을 못 잤어요.
남자 친구를 처음 만났을 때 첫인상이 어땠어요?
ko: 일이 과거에 일어났음을 나타내는 선어말 어미.
example_en: My stomach hurt yesterday. So I couldn't sleep.
I had dinner with my colleague yesterday.
What was your first impression when you first met your boyfriend?
example_zh: 昨天肚子疼，所以没睡好。

name: (았/었/였)던
meaning: Indicates an verb in the past has completed in the past, with the nuance of recollecting a memory.
examples: 저는 어릴 때 했던 게임을 아직 좋아해요.
ko: 과거에 완료된 일을 회상하며 꾸밀 때 쓰는 관형형 어미.
example_en: The classroom that used to be noisy is very quiet these days.
The house we had lived in was very spacious.
I still like the games I played when I was young
example_zh: 曾经吵闹的教室如今非常安静。

name: (았/었/였)었
meaning: Referring to a past event that is different from the present or does not continue to the present.
examples: 이 아빠가 군대 있을 때 취사병이었다고 얘기했었나?
ko: 과거의 일이 지금은 아님을 나타내는 과거완료 표현.
example_en: I lived abroad until 10 years ago.
I didn't eat green onions when I was young.
Did this dad say he was a cook when he was in the army?
example_zh: 直到10年前我一直住在国外。

name: 아/어서인지
meaning: Suggest a possible reason or cause for a situation, with a hint of uncertainty.
examples: 열심히 공부해서인지 학교에서 좋은 성적을 받고 있어요.
산책하러 공원에 자주 가서인지 기분이 좋아요.
음식을 급하게 먹어서인지 소화가 잘 안 돼요.
그 영화가 재미있어서인지 사람들이 많이 봤어요.
ko: 어쩌면 그래서인지,라는 불확실한 이유를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Perhaps because I'm studying hard, I'm getting good grades at school.
Perhaps because I go to the park often for walks, I feel good.
Perhaps because I ate quickly, I'm having trouble digesting.
Maybe because the movie is interesting, many people watched it.
Perhaps because I didn't sleep enough, I'm tired.
example_zh: 也许是因为学习努力，我在学校成绩很好。

name: 아/어야
meaning: Express a necessity, obligation or a condition that has be completed for something else to realize.
examples: 품질이 좋아야 사람들이 그 물건을 살 거예요.
ko: 그래야만 다른 일이 이루어짐을 나타내는 필수 조건의 어미.
example_en: Since the weather has gotten cold, I should wear warm clothes.
People will buy that product if the quality is good.
It was my mistake, so I have to correct it.
example_zh: 天气变冷了，得穿暖和点。

name: 아/어야지
meaning: Express speaker’s strong intention for oneself or a strong suggestion to someone else.
examples: 영화가 너무 재미있다고 했어. 나도 봐야지.
ko: 강한 의지나 당연한 일을 나타낼 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: I heard the movie is very interesting. I must go see it.
Don't just eat fast food, you've got to eat some vegtables too.
The president is giving a speech so we've got to go see it.
example_zh: 听说那部电影特别好看，我也得去看看。

name: (았/었/했)더니
meaning: Used to narrate a sequence of events observed by the speaker. There is often a nuance that the first clause becomes the cause of the second clause. The subjects of both clauses must be different. Note that the speaker's past self and present self can be considered different subjects, and so first-person narration is possible.
examples: 어제 오랜만에 하체를 했더니 다리가 너무 아파.
언니가 동생에게 너 괜찮냐고 물어봤더니 눈물이 펑펑 나왔어.
부모님한테 다음에 차로 태워달라고 했어. 그랬더니 알겠다고 하셨어!
ko: 과거에 관찰한 일의 순서나 변화를 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: Yesterday I did leg day for the first time in a while, so now my legs really hurt.
My big sister asked my little sister if she was okay, and then my little sister burst into tears.
I asked my parents if they could drive me next time. And they said they would!
example_zh: 昨天久违地练了腿，腿疼得不行。

name: 으나
meaning: Expressing contrast or an unexpected outcome.
examples: 이 음식은 건강에 좋으나 맛이 조금 밍밍해요.
새로운 게임은 흥미롭으나 버그가 많아서 플레이하기 어렵네요.
이 옷은 세련되나 가격이 너무 비싸요.
그 박사님은 매우 뛰어나시나 가끔 기본적인 예의를 잊어요.
코드를 간결하게 짰으나 여전히 에러가 발생해요.
숙제를 열심히 했으나 선생님께 칭찬받지 못했어요.
전시된 작품은 다양하나 생각보다 관람객이 적었어요.
이 김치는 전통적이나 너무 매워서 먹기 힘들어요.
그 정치인은 유명하나 실질적인 변화를 이끌지 못해요.
ko: 앞뒤 내용이 대립하거나 뜻밖의 결과임을 나타내는 문어체 어미.
example_en: This food is healthy, but it's a bit bland.
The new game is interesting, but it has so many bugs that it’s hard to play.
This outfit is stylish, but it’s too expensive.
The doctor is a genius, but sometimes forgets basic manners.
I wrote the code concisely, but errors still occur.
I worked hard on my homework, but I didn’t receive any praise from the teacher.
There were a variety of works on display, but there were fewer visitors than I expected.
I exercise every day, but my weight isn’t going down.
This kimchi is traditional, but it’s too spicy to eat.
The politician is famous, but fails to bring about real change.
example_zh: 这个食物有益健康，但味道有点淡。

name: (으)나마
meaning: Expresses the speaker's reluctant acceptance of a situation as-is, even though it is not entirely satisfactory.
ko: 만족스럽지 않아도 그대로 받아들임을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: I'm glad at least you came.
Even though it's a meal without side dishes, please eat your fill.
I was happy to see it, even if only from a distance.
It’s nothing special, but please help yourself.
Although it's late, I'd like to extend my greetings.
example_zh: 好歹你来了，真是万幸。

name: (으/이)니
