meaning: A casual interrogative ending in Korean, often used in informal speech to ask questions. Appear at the end of the sentence and only as 니.
examples: 넌 어느 게 더 비싸 보이니?
ko: 일상 대화에서 쓰이는 반말 의문 종결 어미.
example_en: Which one looks more expensive to you?
How many breads did you buy?
Are you busy these days?
example_zh: 你觉得哪个看起来更贵？

name: (으/이)니
meaning: When the preceding statement is the cause or reason for the next statement or convey a fact.
ko: 앞의 말이 뒤의 말에 대한 원인이나 이유가 됨을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: Since we don't have time, let's move quickly.
Since today's class is over, you can go back.
example_zh: 没时间了，我们快走吧。

name: (으)니까
meaning: It expresses the reason or cause for something. Commonly used to explain the reason for one’s actions or to express to provide justification for something.
examples: 이번 주는 바쁘니까 다음 주에 합시다.
ko: 어떤 일의 이유나 원인을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: I'm busy this week, so let's do that next week.
example_zh: 这周很忙，下周再做吧。

name: (으)니까
meaning: It expresses the discovery of a fact or situation. The first clause is the action and the second clause is about the discovery. This form can only be used with action verbs.
examples: 어제 백화점에 가니까 세일을 하고 있었어요.
ko: 어떤 사실이나 상황을 발견했음을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: When I went to the office in the morning, no one was there.
When I went to the department store yesterday, they were having a sale.
example_zh: 早上到公司一看，一个人都没有。

name: (으)되
meaning: Introduces some truth but adds a contrasting fact, details, conditions, or restrictions.
examples: 한국 드라마를 당연히 보시되 영어 자막만 쓰지 마셔요.
ko: 어떤 사실을 인정하면서 반대되는 사실이나 조건을 덧붙이는 어미.
example_en: Watch K-dramas, of course, just don't use English subtitles.
I have the money, but not the time to spend it...
example_zh: 看韩剧当然可以，只是别用英文字幕。

name: (으)되
meaning: Introduces a direct quote.
ko: 직접 인용을 이끄는 옛말투의 어미.
example_en: The king said, "let him in!"
example_zh: 国王说道：「让他进来！」

name: (으)랴
meaning: Used to enumerate several actions that the speaker is trying hard to complete and the negative effect on the speaker, such as being tired or busy.
examples: 음식 만들랴 집안 청소하랴 쉴 틈이 없다.
어학당에서 공부하랴 회사에 다니랴 눈 코 뜰 새 없어요.
zh: 又要……又要……（忙得不可开交）
ko: 여러 가지 일을 하느라 바쁘고 힘든 상황을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: Between preparing food and cleaning the house, I can't get a second of rest.
I'm busy as a bee between studying at language school and working at my job.
example_zh: 又要做饭又要打扫屋子，一刻不得闲。

name: (으)랴
meaning: Used in informal language to forcefully and ironically support or refute an idea. Very similar to the rhetorical use of -겠어(요).
ko: 이치에 비추어 그럴 수 없다고 반문하는 표현.
example_en: Would you spit on a smiling face? (You can't treat someone badly who treats you well)
Who would turn down money?
Would a carefully-built tower collapse? (If you put all of your effort into what you do, the result cannot possibly be bad)
example_zh: 哪能朝笑脸吐口水呢。（不能亏待对自己好的人）

name: (으)러
meaning: Express a movement toward a location in order to perform the action. Used with verbs of movement.
examples: 나 지금 도서관에 책 빌리러 가는데 같이 갈래?
ko: 이동 동사와 함께 그 목적을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: I'm going to the library to borrow a book, do you want to come with me?
My younger sibling is going to the academy to learn piano.
I'm going to the theater to watch a performance.
example_zh: 我现在去图书馆借书，要不要一起去？

name: (으)려고
meaning: Express an intention, desire or purpose to do something. The speaker will do what is stated in the second clause for the purpose of the first clause.
examples: 누나가 유학을 가려고 학교를 알아보는 중이에요.
ko: 뒤 동작의 의도나 목적을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: I'm learning Korean in order to watch dramas.
Grandfather got up to pick up the fishing rod.
My sister is looking into schools because she's planning to study abroad.
example_zh: 为了看韩剧，我正在学韩语。

name: (으/ㄹ/을)려나
meaning: Expresses curiosity, speculation or doubt to oneself about a future situation or outcome.
examples: 언제 내 집에서 나갈 수 있을려나?
ko: 앞으로의 일에 대해 스스로 궁금하거나 추측할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: I wonder if it will rain.
I wonder if they'll be late?
I wonder when they'll leave my house?
I wonder if the weather will be good tomorrow?
example_zh: 会下雨吗？

name: (으)려다가
meaning: Contraction of -(으)려고 하다가. Express that the speaker intended or tried to do something, but "interrupted" the intention or attempt by doing something else, leaving the original intention unfulfilled.
examples: 그 영화를 DVD 대여점에서 빌려 보려다가 텔레비전에서 오늘 방영한다는 것을 알고는 그만두었다.
몇 년 전 우리 어머니는 병원에서 다른 입원환자를 죽이려다가 붙잡혔어.
ko: ~하려고 했지만 그만두고 달라짐을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I intended to rent that movie from a DVD store, but decided not to when I learned that it will be broadcast tonight on TV.
I thought about knocking on the door, but stopped myself.
A few years ago, my mother tried to kill another patient at the hospital but was caught.
example_zh: 本打算在影碟店租那部电影，后来听说今晚电视要播，就作罢了。

name: (으)려던
meaning: Express that the action or intention was about to happens but got interrupted to change to something else.
examples: 라면을 끓이는군요. 저도 마침 라면을 먹으려던 참이었어요.
저도 백화점에 가려던 참이었는데 같이 가요.
ko: 하려던 일이 중단되고 다른 일로 바뀜을 나타내는 관형형 표현.
example_en: I see you're making ramen, I was just about to eat ramen too.
I was just about to go to the department store too, let's go together.
example_zh: 你在煮拉面啊，我正好也正要吃拉面呢。

name: (으)려면
meaning: Shortened form of (으)려고 하면. Used when the speaker assumes that one wishes to achieve something and gives the conditions and requirements to achieve it.
examples: 덜렁대는 버릇을 고치려면 어떻게 해야 할까요?
다음 마술을 하려면 여러분 중 한 명이 필요합니다.
ko: ~하려면,의 뜻으로 조건을 제시하는 표현.
example_en: What should I do to fix my habit of being indecisive?
We need one of you to volunteer to do the next magic trick.
example_zh: 要改掉毛手毛脚的习惯，该怎么做呢？

name: (으)렴 / (으)려무나 / (으)려마
meaning: Used to give a soft command or suggestion among those who are younger. The extended form also appears as 려므나, however this is not standard korean.
examples: 조용히 앉으려무나 수업이 곧 시작될 거야.
잘 놀았으니 이제 공부를 열심히 하려므나.
ko: 아랫사람에게 부드럽게 명령하거나 권할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Please eat.
Go to bed early.
Please wait a little longer.
Walk slowly; there's no need to rush.
Let's exercise; you'll become healthier.
Hurry up and get ready, there's no time.
Sit quietly, the class will begin soon.
You’ve had plenty of fun, so study hard now.
example_zh: 快吃饭吧。

name: (으)렷다
meaning: Expresses a conjecture or assertion that something is undoubtedly true based on experience or logic.
ko: 경험이나 이치에 비추어 틀림없다고 단정하는 옛말투 어미.
example_en: He won't be complaining again.
You must've finished the book by now.
Judging by his appearance, he can’t be more than 25.
example_zh: 他再也不敢多嘴了。

name: (으)렷다
meaning: Expresses a command or order.
ko: 명령이나 요구를 나타내는 옛말투 어미.
example_en: Don't ever show your face here again.
Bind that criminal at once.
example_zh: 不准再出现在我面前。

name: (으)리
meaning: Expresses the speaker's prediction or guess about some situation. Can be used in pairing with other conjugations or used alone as a verb final ending.
examples: 그는 뭐든 열심히 일하니 꼭 성공하리라.
내일이면 늦으리니 빨리 대책을 세워야 할 것이다.
사노라면 슬픈 날도 있겠지만 즐거운 날도 있으리다.
그 사람이 그런 짓을 하리라고는 상상도 못했어요.
자신은 그녀에게 아주 소중한 친구이리라는 자신감이 있었다.
ko: 어떤 상황에 대한 추측이나 짐작을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: That guy works hard at everything so he’s bound to succeed.
Tomorrow will be too late, so we'll have to come up with a plan quickly.
As you go through life there may be sad days, but there will certainly be happy days too.
The azaleas must be in full bloom back home now.
I couldn't even imagine that he would do such a thing.
He was confident that she considered him a precious friend.
example_zh: 他做什么都那么努力，一定会成功的。

name: (으)리
meaning: Expresses the speaker's intention or will to do something. Can be used in pairing with other conjugations or used alone as a verb final ending. When used as a final ending, can be used to ask about the listener's intention.
examples: 잠시 기다리면 내가 곧 처리해 주리다.
내 반드시 돌아오리니 꼭 기다려 다오.
ko: 말하는 사람의 의지나 뜻을 나타내는 어미.
example_en: If you wait a moment I will take care of it right away.
I will definitely come back, so please wait for me.
I'll take care of the rest.
Should I eat first?
example_zh: 你稍等，我马上处理。

name: (으)리
meaning: Used to respond back with a question, asking how something could be so based on reason. This meaning is only used alone as a verb final ending.
ko: 이치에 비추어 그럴 수 없다고 되묻는 표현.
example_en: How could someone like that be a patriot?
How could I ever do such a thing?
example_zh: 那种人算什么爱国者？

name: (으)리라
meaning: Expresses the speaker's resolve or intention to do something.
ko: 말하는 사람의 결심이나 의지를 나타내는 어미.
example_en: I will definitely succeed.
I am determined to try until the end.
This time, I will surely succeed.
example_zh: 我必定成功。

name: (으)리라
meaning: Make a strong guess or prediction about future events.
ko: 앞으로의 일을 강하게 추측하는 어미.
example_en: Summer shall come soon.
The sun will rise soon.
She will probably succeed.
The truth will come out.
example_zh: 夏天很快就会到来。

name: (으)리만치
meaning: Very similar to -ㄹ 정도로 or -ㄹ 만큼 (but less common), it expresses the extent of a verb or adjective.
examples: 우연치고는 너무 이상하리만치 자꾸 엮이는 것 같아요.
선뜩하리만치 깔끔한 공중제비로, 아이돌이 무대 왼 구석에서 튀어나왔다.
ko: 그 정도에 이를 만큼의 정도를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: We keep running into each other -- it's too strange to be just a coincidence.
The idol burst out from the left corner of the stage with a shockingly/chillingly clean acrobatic move.
example_zh: 我们总是碰面，奇怪得不像巧合。

name: (으)리오
meaning: Emphasize that something is impossible or unlikely by asking a rhetorical question.
ko: 불가능하거나 믿기지 않음을 반문으로 나타내는 옛 표현.
example_en: How could I forget my home?
Who would hate you?
How could we have given up?
Could he possibly succeed?
example_zh: 我怎能忘记故乡。

name: (으)마
meaning: Used when the speaker promises to the listener that they will do something. Very similar to (으)ㄹ게(요).
ko: 약속할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: I'll go in the morning.
I'll help you.
example_zh: 我上午去。

name: (으)므로
meaning: Shows the reason for something
examples: 이 프로젝트는 중요하므로 모두가 참여해야 합니다.
회의 시간이 정해졌으므로 모두 제시간에 도착해야 합니다.
ko: 이유를 나타내는 문어체 연결 어미.
example_en: Since this project is important, everyone must participate.
Since time is limited, we will start the meeting promptly.
Because the meeting time is set, everyone must arrive on time.
example_zh: 这个项目很重要，所以所有人都必须参与。

name: (으)세
meaning: A way to express a suggestion to do a certain act together in the 하게체 speech level. It can also show up as (스)ㅂ세 in dialect.
examples: 말로만 사죄해서는 쓸모가 없지. 그대가 바라는 것이라면 무엇이든 들어주도록 합세.
ko: 하게체에서 함께 행동하자고 권할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: Let’s do our best.
Let's read this book together.
Let us take care of that.
My just saying sorry isn't enough. If there's anything you want, let's do that.
Let's close the door please.
example_zh: 让我们全力以赴吧。

name: (으)십시오
meaning: An even more polite imperative form used to give instructions or make requests.
ko: 가장 정중하게 지시나 부탁을 나타내는 종결 어미.
example_en: Please get off here.
example_zh: 请在这里下车。

name: (으)오/소
meaning: Used to explain the present action, state, or fact politely in the 하오체 speech level.
ko: 하오체로 현재의 동작·상태·사실을 서술하는 종결 어미.
example_en: The weather is really nice.
I do not believe that.
We are going to the mountain.
There is not much time.
example_zh: 天气真好啊。

name: (으)오/소
meaning: Used when the speaker asks the listener politely in the 하오체 speech level.
ko: 하오체로 정중하게 묻는 종결 어미.
example_en: Where are you going?
Is something the matter?
What are you looking for?
How are you feeling today?
example_zh: 您要去哪儿？

name: (으)오/소
meaning: Semi-formal polite command sentence ending in the 하오체 speech level.
ko: 하오체로 명령하거나 요청하는 종결 어미.
example_en: Please come this way.
Please close the door.
Please be quiet.
Please read the book.
example_zh: 请这边走。

name: (으)오/소
meaning: Used to suggest or propose something with the listener, an intention of doing a certain action together in the 하오체 speech level.
ko: 하오체로 함께 하자고 권하는 종결 어미.
example_en: Let's have a meal together.
Let's eat together.
Let's do this work together.
Let's take a walk.
example_zh: 我们一起用餐吧。

name: (으)오/소
meaning: Semi-formal polite sentence ending in the 하오체 speech level with honorific.
ko: 하오체에 존대를 더한 종결 어미.
example_en: Please stay healthy.
Please be happy.
Please live long.
Please be careful.
example_zh: 请保重身体。

name: (으)오/(으)옵/사오/사옵/자오/자옵
meaning: Used to express humility and additional politeness in the 하소서체 speech level. 사옵 and 자옵 are occasionally shortened to 삽 and 잡 respectively.
examples: 필요한 거 있으시다면 저를 불러 주시옵소서.
ko: 하소서체에서 겸손과 높임을 나타내는 옛 종결 어미.
example_en: We don't have that here.
Please call me if you need anything.
We trusted them, but they betrayed us.
I believe in you, so cheer up.
I shall follow my teacher’s will.
We trust in and follow you.
We await your instructions.
example_zh: 我们这儿没有那种东西。

name: (으)오이까/사오이까
meaning: Used to ask a question politely and respectfully in the 하소서체 speech level.
ko: 하소서체에서 정중하게 질문할 때 쓰는 옛 표현.
example_en: Surely there is no such person in this village?
Did you truly win fairly?
Is that really so important?
Who are you looking for, sir?
example_zh: 这村里哪会有这样的人呢？

name: (으)오이다/사오이다
meaning: Used to express an action or simple statement humbly in the 하소서체 speech level.
examples: 아비가 산삼 효험으로 병은 좀 나았사오나 소인 옥에 있는 동안에 죽었소이다.
ko: 하소서체로 겸손하게 진술할 때 쓰는 옛 표현.
example_en: I'm heading out.
My father’s illness improved somewhat thanks to the wild ginseng, but he passed away while I was in prison.
We have a mission to fulfill.
There’s a stranger looking for you.
It’s been quite a while.
I am leaving today.
example_zh: 我就先告辞了。

name: (으)옵시/사옵시/자옵시
meaning: Used to express humility and additional politeness in the 하소서체 speech level.
examples: 부모님의 은혜는 깊으옵시어 갚을 길이 없어라.
ko: 하소서체에서 권유나 명령을 나타내는 옛 표현.
example_en: My parents' favour is so deep I cannot repay it.
He was astonished to hear what I had to say.
The castellan is visiting.
example_zh: 父母恩深似海，无以为报。

name: (으)이/의
meaning: Used to express an impression or a simple description in the 하게체 speech level. Can be shortened from (으)이 to just 의.
ko: 하게체로 인상이나 느낌을 나타내는 옛 표현.
example_en: That's really great.
The weather is quite cold lately.
Your skills are really amazing.
I'm done with that kind of thing.
That's clever, you really had a great idea.
example_zh: 那真是太好了。

name: (으)ㄴ가(요), 나(요)
meaning: It can be use to ask a question in a polite and gentle way.
ko: 정중하고 부드럽게 질문할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: Do you guys also happen to meditate?
Can I get a refund for this?
Are there many people waiting now?
Where are you going to send this package?
example_zh: 各位也偶尔冥想吗？

name: (으)ㄴ가(요), 나(요)
meaning: Expresses the speaker's speculation, curiosity or assumption about something.
examples: 그 아이는 자라면 언젠가 범인이 되나?
내가 좋은 사람인가? 정말 이게 옳은 길이나?
ko: 정중하고 부드럽게 질문할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: When that kid grows up, I wonder if they'll become a criminal someday.
Am I a good person? Is this really the right path?
example_zh: 那孩子长大后会不会哪天变成罪犯呢？

name: (은/ㄴ)들
meaning: Expresses that even if the conditions of the preceding clause are true, the result will not be as expected. Can be used along with -겠어(요) as a rhetorical question.
examples: 돈을 많이 번들 저금하기만 하고 안 쓰면 아무 소용이 없지 않나요?
그 목격자가 경찰에 사실대로 말한다면, 용의자가 아무리 부인한들 형사는 믿어주지 않을 것이다.
사전이 아무리 가까이 있다 한들 그것을 찾아보지 않으면 사전 속의 지식은 남의 머릿속에 든 지식일 뿐이다.
집이 좁은들 우리가 살 수 없겠어?
ko: 그렇다 하더라도 예상대로 되지 않음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Even if you make a lot of money, if you only save it and never use it, isn't it worthless?
If that witness tells the police the truth, then no matter how much the suspect denies it, the detectives won't believe him.
No matter how close a dictionary may be, if you don't use it, the knowledge inside that dictionary is merely knowledge in someone else's head.
Can we not live in a small house? (of course we're able to live in a small house)
example_zh: 就算赚了很多钱，光存着不花，不也没有用吗？

name: (으)ㄹ걸(요)
meaning: Used when stating an unconfirmed assumptions or supposition about a something unsure or a future event.
examples: 출퇴근 시간이니까 지하철을 타는 게 더 빠를걸요.
아이들이 매운 요리는 잘 먹지 않을걸요.
ko: 확실하지 않은 일을 추측할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: Since it's rush hour, I think it would be faster to take the subway.
I don't think kids would eat spicy food well.
example_zh: 现在是上下班高峰，坐地铁应该更快。

name: (으)ㄹ게(요)
meaning: Used when the speaker promises or notifies the listener of their decision or intention that they will do something.
examples: 지금은 비가 많이 오니까 조금 이따가 출발할게요.
ko: 화자의 약속이나 결심을 나타내는 종결 어미.
example_en: I will answer the phone.
Since it's raining a lot now, I will leave a little later.
example_zh: 我来接电话。

name: (으)ㄹ까
meaning: Used to make a suggestion to the listener, sometime with the intent of doing something together.
ko: 함께 하자고 제안할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: It's raining a lot. Shall we take a taxi?
Where shall we take a picture?
example_zh: 雨下得很大，要不要打车？

name: (으)ㄹ까
meaning: Ask the for listener's preference, thought or opinion.
ko: 상대의 생각이나 의견을 물을 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: What time shall I call you?
Do you think there will be a lot of people at the department store today?
The air is bad. Shall I close the window?
example_zh: 我几点给你打电话好呢？

name: (으)ㄹ까
meaning: Wondering to oneself, considering a possbility or action.
ko: 혼자 속으로 짐작하며 궁금해하는 표현.
example_en: I wonder if this will taste good?
Should I go to the market today?
So then... hmm... what am I trying to say (how should I put it)? Nevermind, it doesn't matter.
example_zh: 这个会好吃吗？

name: (으)ㄹ꼬
meaning: Ask for the listener's or one's own preference, thought or opinion.
ko: 상대나 자신의 생각을 물을 때 쓰는 옛 표현.
example_en: Young-hee, what song are you going to sing?
When are we leaving?
Why is this room so small?
example_zh: 英熙，你要唱什么歌呀？

name: (으)ㄹ꼬
meaning: Wondering to oneself, expressing conjecture or speculation.
ko: 상대나 자신의 생각을 물을 때 쓰는 옛 표현.
example_en: What am I going to do to make a living now?
With no home, where am I supposed to go?
I wonder where he went?
example_zh: 今后我该怎么谋生呢？

name: (으)ㄹ라
meaning: Expresses concern that what was just mentioned might happen.
examples: 우리는 가지 말자, 그 귀찮은 놈도 왔을라.
ko: 그렇게 될까 걱정할 때 쓰는 구어 표현.
example_en: Shush! He might look this way.
Don't run so fast, you might get hurt.
Let's not go, that annoying guy is probably there too.
example_zh: 嘘！他可能会朝这边看。

name: (으)ㄹ라치면
meaning: Expresses that every time some action tries to happen, it results in another action to happen. Equivalent to -으려고 할 때마다 or -으려고 하면.
examples: 무슨 BL 드라마를 볼라치면 어머니가 내 방에 들어오셔.
분위기가 어색할라치면 얘가 재밌는 농담을 하거든.
ko: 하려고 할 때마다 다른 일이 생김을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Whenever I try to watch some BL drama, my mom comes into my room.
Every time the atmosphere becomes awkward he cracks a funny joke, y'know.
Every time I study, my friend sends me a message on KakaoTalk.
example_zh: 每次想看什么BL剧，我妈就进我房间。

name: (으)ㄹ래(요)
meaning: Used to indicate the speaker's intention to do something in the future.
examples: 어른이 되면 우선 운전 면허를 딸래요.
ko: 화자의 의향을 나타내거나 상대의 뜻을 물을 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: When I become an adult, I will get a driver's license first.
I'll have a cup of black tea.
example_zh: 成年后我要先考驾照。

name: (으)ㄹ래(요)
meaning: To ask for the listener's thoughts about the thing to do in the future.
examples: 내일 시간이 있으면 같이 영화를 볼래요?
ko: 화자의 의향을 나타내거나 상대의 뜻을 물을 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: If you have time tomorrow, how about watching a movie together?
How about having lunch together today?
example_zh: 明天有时间的话，要不要一起看电影？

name: (으)ㄹ망정 / (으)ㄹ지언정
meaning: Acknowledge or assume the truth of the first part and emphasize a contrasting fact in the second.
examples: 그는 나를 돕지는 못할망정 방해는 하지 말아야지요.
친구가 이해는 못해줄망정 비난은 하지 않았으면 좋겠어요.
오늘이 삶의 끝일지언정 후회 없는 하루를 보내도록 하겠다
그는 지키지는 못할지언정 약속은 함부로 하지 않아요.
ko: 앞 내용을 인정하면서 뒤의 대립되는 내용을 강조하는 표현.
example_en: Even though he can't help me, he shouldn't hinder me.
Even if my friend can't understand, I hope they don't criticize.
Even if today were the end of my life, I would live it without regrets.
Even if he can't keep it, he doesn't make promises lightly.
example_zh: 他就算帮不了我，也不该妨碍我。

name: (으)ㄹ밖에
meaning: Used when there is no other choice but the preceding state/action. This is an informal version of :grammar[을_수밖에_없다].
ko: 그 방법 외에 다른 길이 없음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Since all the adults have left, I guess I have to go too.
The teacher's telling me to do it, so I have to.
If the owner tells me to hand it over, I’ll have no choice but to do so.
example_zh: 大人们都走了，我也只能跟着去。

name: (으)ㄹ세
meaning: Used to express the speaker's thoughts or conjecture in the 하게체 speech level.
examples: 내 가게 문 닫으면 그 자가 춤출세.
ko: 하게체로 자신의 생각이나 추측을 서술하는 종결 어미.
example_en: If my shop closes, that guy will be dancing for joy.
This painting is really nice.
"Who is it?" "It's me."
example_zh: 我的店一关门，那家伙就该高兴得跳舞了。

name: (으)ㄹ세
meaning: Express admiration after realizing something new, in the 하게체 speech level.
ko: 하게체로 새삼 깨달은 것을 감탄하듯 말하는 종결 어미.
example_en: Oh my, that’s today.
Wow, that’s a great idea.
example_zh: 哎呀，那不就是今天嘛。

name: (으)ㄹ세
meaning: Express intention in the 하게체 speech level.
ko: 하게체로 자신의 의지를 나타내는 종결 어미.
example_en: I'll let you know later then. Take care.
We'll eat together once father arrives.
example_zh: 那我回头告诉你。慢走。

name: (으)ㄹ수록
meaning: The more you do something, the more another thing happens.
ko: 하면 할수록 더해짐을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: The faster you walk, the more tired you get.
The more often we meet, the closer we become.
The earlier you sleep, the healthier you are.
example_zh: 走得越快，越累。

name: (으)ㄹ지(도)
meaning: Used to indicate the speaker's vague doubt.
examples: 내일 있을 중요한 시험을 잘 볼 수 있을지 걱정이 되어 잠을 설쳤다.
ko: 확실하지 않음을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: I was worried about the important exam tomorrow and couldn't sleep.
example_zh: 担心明天的重要考试能不能考好，一夜没睡好。

name: (으)ㅁ
meaning: Turns verbs or adjectives into abstract nouns representing a concept or idea.
ko: 동사·형용사를 추상적인 개념 명사로 만드는 명사형 어미.
example_en: Death is frightening.
Faith is an important value.
Lack of sleep causes harm to health.
example_zh: 死亡令人恐惧。

name: (으)ㅁ
meaning: Turns verbs or adjectives into nouns, often used in formal writing to state facts or make lists.
ko: 동사·형용사를 명사로 만들어 사실을 서술하거나 나열하는 명사형 어미.
example_en: Studying is enjoyable.
I inform you that I couldn't attend.
I report that the problem has been solved.
example_zh: 学习是快乐的。

name: (으)ㅁ
meaning: Used at the end of sentences in formal writing to state facts or conclusions.
ko: 글말에서 사실이나 결론을 맺을 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: I will conclude the report here.
All preparations have been completed.
example_zh: 报告到此结束。

name: (으)ㅁ세
meaning: Expresses the speaker's enthusiastic intention to do something in the 하게체 speech level.
ko: 하게체로 의욕을 나타내는 종결 어미.
example_en: I'll eat soon!
I'll take care of that.
I'll get you a coffee.
example_zh: 我马上就吃饭！

name: (으)ㅂ시다
meaning: Used to suggest or propose something with the listener, an intention of doing a certain action together.
examples: 제가 매운 음식을 못 먹으니까 다른 음식을 먹읍시다.
ko: 함께 행동하자고 제안할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: The view is nice. Let's take a picture here.
Since I can't eat spicy food, let's eat something else.
The road is blocked. Let's take a taxi.
example_zh: 风景真好，我们在这里拍张照吧。

name: (이)라서
meaning: Used for a reason or cause.
examples: 달리기 시합이 아니라서 제가 달리고 싶은 속도로 달릴 수 있어요.
제가 임산부라서 그러는데 이 자리에 앉아도 될까요?
ko: '이다'의 이유나 근거를 나타내는 연결 표현.
example_en: I have to go to my hometown because it's my mother's birthday.
It's not a running competition, so I can run at the speed I want.
I'm pregnant, so can I sit here?
example_zh: 因为今天是母亲的生日，我得回老家。

name: 자
meaning: A way to express a suggestion to do a certain act together.
examples: 회사 끝나면 술 한 잔 하자.
ko: 함께하자고 제안하는 연결 어미.
example_en: Let's eat grilled fish to our heart's content tonight!
Let's have a drink after work.
example_zh: 今晚烤鱼管够吃！

name: 자
meaning: Indicates that the second action occurs **as** or **when** the first action is happening.
examples: 차에서 연기가 나자 운전사는 차에서 뛰쳐나왔다.
ko: 함께하자고 제안하는 연결 어미.
example_en: As I opened the window, the wind came in.
I fell asleep as I sat down.
The driver rushed out of the car as smoke started coming out of it.
example_zh: 窗户一开，风就吹了进来。

name: 자고
meaning: Used to indirectly convey someone's recommendation or suggestion.
examples: 남자 친구가 주말에 극장에서 영화를 보자고 해요.
ko: 남의 제안이나 권유를 간접적으로 전할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Dad suggested we eat.
They suggested we meet this weekend.
My boyfriend suggested we watch a movie at the theater this weekend.
example_zh: 爸爸说一起吃饭吧。

name: 자꾸나
meaning: A way to express a suggestion to do a certain act together. This is identical in meaning to :grammar[verb_자]{suggestion}, but carries a more intimate tone.
examples: 너만 먹지 말고 나도 좀 먹자꾸나.
ko: 계속하자고 반복하여 권할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Don't just eat it all yourself, let me have some too.
Let’s work even harder.
Let's hang out.
example_zh: 别光你自己吃，也让我吃点嘛。

name: 자마자
meaning: Indicates that something happens immediately at the end of an action.
ko: 앞 동작이 끝나자마자 뒤 동작이 일어남을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: The weather got cold as soon as the rain stopped.
The children ran out of the room as soon as the bell rang.
example_zh: 雨一停，天就变冷了。

name: 잖아
meaning: Indicates that the speaker is reminding the listener of a reason they should be aware or might have forgotten.
examples: 지하철을 탑시다. 출퇴근 시간에는 차가 많이 밀리잖아요.
그렇게 싸우지 말고 사이좋게 지내. 둘이 친구잖아.
ko: 상대가 알거나 잊은 이유를 일깨워 줄 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Let's take the subway. There surely are a lot of traffic during rush hours.
Don't fight like that and get along well. You two are friends, you know.
example_zh: 坐地铁吧。上下班高峰期路上肯定很堵的呀。

name: 지
meaning: Used when the speaker want to confirm an already known fact with the listener or obtains the listener's agreement.
examples: 설마 그 사람이랑 다시 사귀고 싶은 건 아니지?
ko: 알고 있는 사실을 확인하거나 동의를 구할 때 쓰는 종결 어미.
example_en: You don't want to get back together with that person, do you?
example_zh: 你不会还想和那个人复合吧？

name: 지만
meaning: Express a contrast between two clauses and the second clause is usually a contrast to the first clause.
ko: 앞뒤 내용이 대립함을 나타내는 연결 어미.
example_en: It's a bit expensive, but it's still very delicious.
I warned you, but it's dangerous.
example_zh: 虽然有点贵，但还是很好吃。

name: (으)ㄹ 것이다
meaning: Used to express a future plan.
examples: 나는 주말에 집에서 푹 쉴 거야.
ko: 앞으로의 계획이나 추측을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I will go to school tomorrow.
Where will you sell it?
I will go on a picnic on Saturday.
I will rest at home on the weekend.
example_zh: 我明天要去学校。

name: (으)ㄹ 것이다
meaning: Expresses the speaker's supposition about a certain situation based on something heard, seen or personal experience.
examples: 공사를 하는 동안 좀 시끄러울 거예요.
ko: 앞으로의 계획이나 추측을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I think he will like a smartphone as a birthday present.
It will be noisy while they are doing construction.
example_zh: 生日礼物的话，我觉得他会喜欢智能手机。

name: 을/를 바라다
meaning: Used to express the speaker's hope or wish for something to happen.
examples: 여러분의 성공을 기원하며 행복한 미래를 가지시길 바랍니다.
ko: ~하기를 바란다는 뜻을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I hope for your success and wish you a happy future.
I hope everyone returns safely.
I hope for everyone's happiness.
example_zh: 祝愿各位取得成功，拥有幸福的未来。

name: (으)ㄹ 뻔하다
meaning: Indicate one's relief that a past event almost happened but did not.
examples: 친구와 통화하다가 음식을 다 태울 뻔했어요.
네가 전화하지 않았더라면 약속을 잊어버릴 뻔했어요.
ko: 하마터면 그럴 뻔했지만 다행히 아니었음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I was talking with my friend on the phone and almost burned all my food.
If you hadn't called me, I would have forgotten the appointment.
It was so cold, I almost die.
example_zh: 和朋友打电话，差点把菜全烧糊了。

name: (으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다
meaning: A pattern to expresses when someone is able to do something or when something is possible.
examples: 저는 그 사실을 믿을 수 없어요.
ko: 능력이나 가능성을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I can drive.
I can't believe that.
example_zh: 我会开车。

name: (으)ㄹ 수도 있다/없다
meaning: Expresses that such a possibility also exists.
examples: 저 내일 시간이 없을 수도 있어요.
그렇게 많은 돈을 가지고 있는 것을 상상할 수도 없어요.
ko: 그런 가능성도 있거나 없음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I might not have time tomorrow.
My friend might come.
I can't even imagine having that much money.
example_zh: 我明天可能没时间。

name: 거나 말거나
meaning: Conveys a strong decision that something will happen regardless of the situation.
examples: 그녀가 이번 연구를 끝내거나 말거나 이미 많은 여성들한테 롤 모델이 되고 있어요.
새로운 영화를 보러 가거나 말거나 책 읽는 게 아이디어 얻는 데 더 좋대요
새로운 취미를 찾거나 말거나 일단 지금까지 하던 걸 계속할 거예요.
다이어트를 하거나 말거나 어쨌든 살은 이미 빠졌어요.
ko: 상황과 관계없이 반드시 그렇게 함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Whether she finishes the research or not, she’s already a role model for many women.
Whether she goes to watch the new movie or not, she says reading is better for getting ideas.
Whether she finds a new hobby or not, she’s going to keep doing what she’s been doing.
Whether she goes on a diet or not, she’s already lost weight anyway.
example_zh: 不管她这次研究能不能完成，她已经是许多女性的榜样了。

name: 건 말건
meaning: Conveys a strong decision that something will happen regardless of the situation in a casual way.
examples: 비가 오건 말건 산책은 할 거예요.
사람들이 이해하건 말건 제 생각은 바꾸지 않을 거예요.
시험 결과가 좋건 말건 최선을 다한 걸로 만족해요.
친구가 오건 말건 파티 음식은 준비해 놓을게요.
어머니가 허락하건 말건 여행 계획은 진행할 거예요.
ko: 상황과 관계없이 강한 결심을 나타내는 구어 표현.
example_en: Whether it rains or not, I’ll go out for a walk.
Whether people understand or not, I won’t change my opinion.
Whether the exam results are good or not, I’m satisfied I did my best.
Whether my friend comes or not, I’ll prepare the party food.
Whether my mom approves or not, I’ll proceed with the travel plans.
example_zh: 不管下不下雨，我都要去散步。

name: 게 되다
meaning: Expresses a change from one state to another or a change in situation as a result of someone else's action or the environment, regardless of the will of the subject.
examples: 저는 버섯을 안 먹었었는데 먹게 됐어요.
ko: 상황의 변화나 결과를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I became good at cooking.
I came to like soccer.
I didn't eat mushrooms, but I ended up eating them.
example_zh: 我做菜做得好了。

name: 게 하다
meaning: Used to express that the speaker caused, influenced or let someone do something
examples: 부모님이 제가 더 건강하게 살게 하셨어요.
ko: 남에게 어떤 일을 하게 함을 나타내는 사동 표현.
example_en: The teacher made the students study hard.
My parents made me live more healthily.
I made my child clean his room.
example_zh: 老师让学生们努力学习。

name: 고 나니(까)
meaning: Indicates that an action or event happens after another action or event but with a reason or cause.
examples: 요리를 하고 나니까 주방이 매우 더러워졌어요.
오랫동안 무언가를 하고 나니 팔이 조금 아프네요.
ko: 일이 끝나고 나서 깨닫게 되었음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: After cooking, the kitchen became very dirty.
After doing something for a long time, my arms hurt a bit.
example_zh: 做完饭一看，厨房变得很脏。

name: 고 나면
meaning: Indicates that an action or event happens after another action or event, but with a conditional relationship.
examples: 일을 다 마치고 나면 집에 갈 거예요.
ko: 일이 끝난 뒤의 조건적 결과를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I will go home after finishing work.
After exercising, I take a shower.
example_zh: 做完事情后我就回家。

name: 고 나서
meaning: Indicates that an action or event happens after another action or event.
examples: 저는 밥을 먹고 나서 숙제를 할 거예요.
저는 저녁을 먹고 나서 텔레비전을 봐요.
ko: 한 동작이 끝난 뒤에 다른 동작이 이어짐을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I will do my homework after eating.
I watch TV after eating dinner.
example_zh: 我吃完饭后要写作业。

name: 고 말겠다
meaning: Expresses the speaker''s strong will or determination to do something or complete an action.
ko: 반드시 해 내고야 말겠다는 강한 의지를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I will definitely make this project a success.
I will uncover the truth no matter what.
I will achieve my goal.
example_zh: 我一定要让这个项目成功。

name: 고 말다
meaning: Expresses that an action happened unintentionally, unexpectedly, or inevitably.
ko: 어쩔 수 없이 그리고야 말았음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I ended up losing my temper.
I ended up telling my friend's secret.
I was on a diet, but I ended up eating cake.
example_zh: 我最后还是没忍住发了火。

name: 고 보니(까)
meaning: Indicates a realization or conclusion after some action or event.
examples: 버스를 타고 보니까 반대 방향으로 가는 것이었어요.
ko: 행동을 해 본 뒤에 비로소 알게 되었음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I got off the subway and found I didn't have my bag with me.
I got on the bus and found it was going in the opposite direction.
example_zh: 下了地铁才发现包不见了。

name: 고 싶다
meaning: Used to express a desire or wish to do something.
ko: ~하고 싶은 소망을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I want to meet a friend.
Last year, I wanted to travel to Korea.
example_zh: 我想见一位朋友。

name: 고 있다
meaning: Expresses that an action is ongoing. This pattern is sometime mentioned as progressive tense.
ko: 동작이 진행 중임을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I am writing an email now.
I am exercising every weekend.
example_zh: 我现在正在写邮件。

name: 곤 하다
meaning: Indicate a habitual action of the present or past.
examples: 밤에 잠이 안 오면 음악을 듣곤 해요.
ko: 과거나 현재의 습관적인 행동을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I use to work out after work at the office.
When I can't sleep at night, I often listen to music
example_zh: 我常在下班后运动。

name: 기 마련이다
meaning: Used to indicate the occurrence of something being natural or inevitable based on common facts or beliefs.
examples: 겨울이 아무리 추워도 봄은 오기 마련이다.
진실은 언젠가 드러나기 마련이니까 어디 두고 봅시다.
ko: 당연히 그리 되기 마련임을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Regardless of how cold winter is, spring will naturally come.
It's inevitable that the truth will come out, so let's wait and see.
example_zh: 冬天再冷，春天也终会到来。

name: 기 일쑤이다
meaning: Used to show that something happens often, usually in a bad way.
ko: 흔히, 특히 좋지 않게, 그리 되곤 함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: My friend often forgets appointments.
My younger sibling often loses things.
example_zh: 我朋友经常忘记约定。

name: 기도 하다
meaning: Used to say sometimes the action happens.
examples: 저는 주말에는 맛있는 음식을 만들어 먹기도 해요.
ko: 그런 일도 있거나 그렇게도 함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Sometimes on weekends, I cook and eat delicious food.
I sometimes watch movies on weekends.
example_zh: 周末我有时会做好吃的吃。

name: 기로 하다
meaning: Used to make a promise with another person or oneself.
examples: 건강 때문에 올해부터 담배를 끊기로 했어요.
ko: 자신이나 남과 약속을 정함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I made the decision to stop smoking for my health from this year.
We've decided to get married three years from now.
example_zh: 为了健康，我决定从今年开始戒烟。

name: 는/(으)ㄴ/(으)ㄹ 것
meaning: Changes the sentence, or the verb phrase of a sentence, into a noun.
ko: 문장이나 동사구를 명사로 바꾸는 표현.
example_en: I like the act of reading books.
We will go next week.
example_zh: 我喜欢读书。

name: 는/(으)ㄴ/(으)ㄹ 것 같다
meaning: Used to express a thought, guess, or assumption that one isn't fully certain of.
examples: 점심 시간이 끝나서 제 친구가 이미 먹은 것 같아요.
ko: 확실하지 않은 생각이나 추측을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: It seems like the weather will be cold.
I think the party will be fun.
It seems/I think there's no one here.
Since lunch time is over, I think my friend has already eaten.
I think/they seem like a good person.
example_zh: 天气好像会变冷。

name: 는 길에
meaning: Expresses that while en route to or from a place, another action takes place.
examples: 친구를 만나러 나가는 길에 책을 반납할 거예요.
ko: 가는 길에 다른 일을 함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I bought bread on my way home.
On my way to the market, I bought some coffee.
On my way out to meet a friend, I will return the book.
On my way out from the office, I stopped by the flower shop.
Shall we stop by the convenience store on the way to the library?
example_zh: 回家路上买了面包。

name: 는 길이다
meaning: Used with motion verbs to indicate that the speaker is currently en route going to or coming from a place.
examples: 목사님이 지금 교회에 오시는 길이라고 했어요.
색연필을 사러 가는 길인데 혹시 필요한 것이 있어요?
제가 지금 집에 가는 길이라서 20분 후에 또 전화하면 안 돼요?
ko: 지금 어디에 가고 오는 중임을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I am on my way home.
I am on my way out of the office.
I am on my way up the mountain.
I’m currently on my way into the hospital.
Yesterday, I was on my way down the mountain.
The reverend said he is on the way to the church now.
I’m heading out to buy some colored pencils, by chance do you need anything?
I am on my way home right now, so can you call me back in 20 minutes?
example_zh: 我正在回家的路上。

name: 는 김에
meaning: Expresses doing another action while doing something else, taking advantage of the situation.
examples: 시장에 가는 김에 새로운 옷을 구경했어요.
모델 촬영을 준비하는 김에 메이크업도 연습했어요.
학교에 가는 김에 도서관에서 책을 빌렸어요.
해변에 가는 김에 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
자동차를 닦는 김에 내부 청소도 했어요.
게임하는 김에 새로운 캐릭터를 만들어 봤어요.
여행 준비하는 김에 비행기 표도 확인했어요.
ko: 어떤 일을 하는 기회에 다른 일도 함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Since I was going to the market anyway, I also browsed some new clothes.
While preparing for the modeling shoot, I also practiced my makeup.
Since I came to Seoul anyway, I stopped by an exhibition.
While I was cleaning, I also sorted out some old books.
Since I was going to school anyway, I borrowed some books from the library.
Since I went to the beach anyway, I took a lot of photos.
Since I was washing the car anyway, I also cleaned the interior.
Since I was studying for the exam anyway, I also organized my notes.
Since I was already playing games, I tried creating a new character.
Since I was preparing for the trip anyway, I also checked the flight tickets.
example_zh: 反正要去市场，顺便看了看新衣服。

name: (으)ㄴ/는 모양이다
meaning: Used to infer or guess a situation after observation.
examples: 하늘을 보니 곧 비가 올 모양이에요.
전화를 안 받는 걸 보니 집에 아무도 없는 모양이에요.
ko: 관찰을 바탕으로 상황을 짐작할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Looking at the sky, it looks like it will rain soon.
It seems that no one is at home because they don't answer the phone.
example_zh: 看天色，好像马上要下雨了。

name: 는 바람에
meaning: Used to indicate that something happened as an unintended consequence or result of a particular action or situation, often with a negative or unexpected outcome.
examples: 전기가 나가는 바람에 TV를 못 봤어요.
ko: 어떤 행동의 탓에 뜻밖의 결과가 생겼음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Because of the rain, we canceled the picnic.
I couldn't watch TV because the power went out.
example_zh: 因为下雨，野餐取消了。

name: 는 반면에
meaning: Used to show that two clauses are contrasting or opposite to each other.
examples: 이 보고서는 이해하기 쉬운 반면에 다른 보고서들은 복잡합니다.
서울의 날씨는 추운 반면에 남쪽 지방은 따뜻합니다.
이 도시는 밤에는 조용한 반면에 낮에는 매우 붐벼요.
ko: 서로 반대되는 두 내용을 대비할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: This report is easy to understand, whereas other reports are complex.
Seoul's weather is cold, whereas the southern regions are warm.
This city is quiet at night, whereas it's very crowded during the day.
example_zh: 这份报告容易理解，而其他报告则很复杂。

name: (으)ㄴ/는 법이다
meaning: Indicates that a certain situation or outcome is expected, natural, or bound to happen.
examples: 싸고 품질이 좋은 물건은 잘 팔리는 법이다.
시간이 지나면 모든 것이 변하는 법이다.
ko: 당연히 그런 결과를 가져옴을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: If you have high expectations, disappointment is inevitable.
Affordable, high-quality products are bound to sell well.
The more you get your hopes up, the more you'll be disappointed.
If you don't make an effort, failure is natural.
Over time, everything is bound to change.
example_zh: 期望越大，失望就越大，这是必然的。

name: (으)ㄴ/는 셈이다
meaning: Expresses that something is practically the same as something else.
examples: 그동안 열심히 준비했으니 거의 합격한 셈이죠.
모델들이 많아 보여도 사실상 없는 셈이에요.
오늘 학교에서 발표를 성공적으로 마친 셈이었어요.
우리가 박물관에서 본 것은 역사를 체험한 셈이에요.
이 과제는 거의 다 한 셈일 거예요.
이번 시험 결과를 보면 다음 학기에 합격한 셈일지도 몰라요.
ko: 실질적으로 그와 같다고 할 수 있음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: It is as though I did well on this shoot.
Since I prepared hard, it is as though I passed the audition.
At this level, it is practically half a success in the industry.
Even though it looks like there are many models, it is as though there are none.
It was as though we successfully finished the presentation at school today.
It was practically as though we enjoyed the trip to Paris with friends.
What we saw at the museum was practically experiencing history.
This assignment is practically done.
Judging by this test result, it might be as though I passed for next semester.
example_zh: 这次拍摄算是拍得相当不错了。

name: (으)ㄴ/는 셈이다
meaning: Indicates that something can be counted, interpreted, or calculated as another thing.
examples: 이 식당의 가격을 생각하면 정말 싼 셈이에요.
이 일을 10년 동안 했으니 이제 전문가인 셈이에요.
하루에 5시간씩 공부하면 한 달에 150시간을 공부한 셈이에요.
일주일에 다섯 번 밖에서 식사하면 거의 매일 외식하는 셈이에요.
ko: 실질적으로 그와 같다고 할 수 있음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Considering the prices of this restaurant, it is really cheap.
Having done this work for 10 years, I am practically an expert.
If you study 5 hours a day, that amounts to studying 150 hours a month.
If you eat out five times a week, it's practically as though you eat out every day.
example_zh: 考虑到这家店的价格，真的算是便宜了。

name: (으)ㄴ/는 편이다
meaning: Expresses a tendency or habit to do or be something.
examples: 저는 다른 사람들보다 커피를 많이 마시는 편이에요.
회사 앞 식당이 음식도 맛있고 가격도 싼 편이에요.
ko: 어느 쪽에 속하는 경향임을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I tend to drink more coffee than other people.
The restaurant in front of the company is good and cheap.
The weather today is rather good.
example_zh: 我和别人相比，咖啡喝得比较多。

name: 다(가) 보니(까)
meaning: Indicates a sudden realization or conclusion after doing an action continuously for quite some time.
examples: 책을 읽다가 보니 시간이 훌쩍 지나갔어요.
한국어를 매일매일 계속 하다 보니까 발음이 알아서 늘더라고요.
ko: 어떤 행동을 계속하다가 새삼 깨닫게 됨을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: While reading the book, I realized time had flown by.
After working for a long time, I noticed that my skills had improved.
I noticed that my pronunciation improved on its own when I kept consistently using Korean every single day.
example_zh: 读书读着读着，发现时间一下子就过去了。

name: 다(가) 보니(까)
meaning: Used with 이다. It provides a reason or background for the following clause.
examples: 열아홉 살이다 보니까 솔직히 유치할 줄 알았는데 생각이 깊더라.
선생님이다 보니까 애들이 쓰는 신조어를 쉽게 배우게 돼요.
판매자가 말하는 가격이 말도 안 되게 비쌌는데, 절실히 필요로 하는 입장이다 보니 잔말 없이 살 수밖에 없었다.
ko: 이다와 함께 쓰여 뒤 절의 이유나 근거를 제시하는 표현.
example_en: Honestly, I thought he would be immature since he's only 19, but it turns out he's a deep thinker.
As a teacher, I can easily pick up the new slang the kids use.
The price the seller gave was insanely expensive, but since I desperately needed it, I couldn't help but buy it without a complaint.
example_zh: 因为才19岁，说实话本以为会很幼稚，没想到思想挺成熟。

name: 다(가) 보면
meaning: Expresses a result that can happen when an action is done consistently for quite some time. Often used in suggestions.
examples: 강력계 형사로 활동하다 보면 위험에 처할 때도 있어서 호신술로 합기도 배웠죠.
그 선배와 함께 일하다 보면 좋은 호텔리어란 뭔지 곧 알게 될 겁니다.
헬스 꾸준히 가다 보면 살 빠질 거예요.
ko: 어떤 일을 계속하면 생기는 결과를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: In my career as a homicide detective, there are times I'm put in danger, so I learned hapkido for self-defense.
If you work with him for a while, you'll come to know what it means to be a good hotelier.
If you keep going to the gym consistently, you'll be able to lose weight.
example_zh: 做重案组刑警，有时会陷入危险，所以学了合气道防身。

name: 다고/라고 치다
meaning: To assume or consider a hypothetical scenario as if it were true.
examples: 모든 학생이 숙제를 마쳤다고 치고 발표를 시작합시다.
그가 이 작품을 이해했다고 치고 설명을 생략할게요.
내일 아침에 운동한다고 치고 일찍 잠자리에 드세요.
코드가 이미 최적화되었다고 치고 테스트를 진행해 봅시다.
그 식단이 효과적이라고 치고 한 달 더 유지해볼까요?
그가 전문가라고 치고 그의 조언을 들어보겠습니다.
ko: 실제가 아니더라도 그렇다고 가정함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Let’s start the presentation assuming all the students finished their homework.
Assuming he understands this piece, I'll skip the explanation.
Let’s assume you’ll work out tomorrow morning, so go to bed early.
Let’s proceed with testing, assuming the code is already optimized.
Assuming that diet is effective, shall we continue it for another month?
Let’s assume he’s an expert and listen to his advice.
example_zh: 假设所有学生都完成了作业，我们开始发表吧。

name: 다시피 하다
meaning: Used to describe a situation where something is almost or practically the same or close to another action, but isn't exactly the same.
examples: 그 남자는 매일 집에서 살다시피 해요.
비가 너무 많이 와서 물에 잠기다시피 했어요.
그 여자는 삼겹살을 주식으로 하다시피 해요.
ko: 거의 그와 다름없음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: He practically lives at home every day.
It rained so much that it was practically flooded.
She practically lives on pork belly as her staple food.
example_zh: 他几乎每天都住在家里的样子。

name: (ㄴ/는)단/(이)란 말
meaning: Used to confirm what the other person said.
ko: 상대가 말한 것을 확인할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Are you saying you're going skiing even though it's cold?
Are you saying you stayed up late yesterday?
Are you saying you're angry with me right now?
example_zh: 你是说天气那么冷还要去滑雪？

name: (ㄴ/는)단/(이)란 말
meaning: Used to emphasize what the speaker said.
ko: 상대가 말한 것을 확인할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: I said try again!
I said do your homework!
I said be quiet!
example_zh: 我说了，重做一遍！

name: 대신(에)
meaning: Indicates an action can be replaced or compensated by another.
ko: 앞의 것을 대신하거나 보상함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Could you order instead of me?
Will you have pizza instead of rice?
example_zh: 能替我点一下单吗？

name: 동안
meaning: Indicates the time period when a certain action begins and lasts until it ends.
ko: 어떤 동작이 시작되어 끝날 때까지의 기간을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Yesterday, I slept for 12 hours.
Bears hibernate during winter.
example_zh: 昨天睡了12个小时。

name: 때
meaning: Expresses the time when an action occurs or its duration.
ko: 동작이 일어난 시간을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I work part-time during vacation.
This is a picture when I was 7 years old.
example_zh: 放假期间我打工。

name: 때문에
meaning: Expresses a reason or cause of a situation.
ko: 어떤 상황의 이유나 원인을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: The road is slippery because of the snow.
I went to the hospital because of the cold.
example_zh: 因为下雪，路很滑。

name: 만 해도
meaning: When following an expression of time (-전, -까지, 때...), expresses that as recently as some point in the past, something was different or not the case.
examples: 10년 전만 해도, 우리 나라가 이렇게 양극화되지는 않았다.
어제까지만 해도 나는 그 사람이 사건에 관여했을 거라고는 생각도 못했어.
도서관에 들어올 때까지만 해도 공부할 의욕이 차고 넘쳐났는데 교과서 펴고 보니까 집중이 안 되더라고요.
누구도 그를 한 달 전까지만 해도 노숙자라고 상상하지 못했을 것이다.
ko: 과거 어느 시점만 해도 그랬음을 강조하는 표현.
example_en: Even just 10 years ago, our country was not this polarized.
Just yesterday, I hadn't even once thought that he could have been involved in this case.
Right up until I entered the library, I was full of motivation to study, but once I opened the textbook, I couldn't focus at all.
I couldn't speak Korean back then. (As recently as that point, I couldn't speak Korean)
No one would have been able to imagine that he had been homeless as recently as a month ago.
example_zh: 就在10年前，我们国家还没有这么两极分化。

name: 아/어 가다
meaning: Indicates an action in the present continues into the future.
examples: 시간이 지나면서, 저는 아버지를 더 닮아 가고 있어요!
살아가면서 힘든 일이 많지만 포기하지 않을 거예요!
ko: 현재의 동작이 앞으로도 계속됨을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I will keep studying Korean! (now and in the future)
Are things going well? / Is work progressing favourably?
As time goes on, I'm looking like my father (more and more)!
As you go through life there are many difficlties, but I won't give up!
example_zh: 我会继续学习韩语的！

name: 아/어 가다
meaning: Indicates an action moves away from the speaker and towards a destination or person.
examples: 집에서 기다려 주세요. 치킨을 사 갈게요.
여기에서 먹어도 안 돼요. 음식을 가져가세요.
ko: 동작이 말하는 사람에게서 멀어져 감을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I walked to the restaurant.
Please wait at home. I'll buy chicken (and go to you.)
You're not allowed to eat here. Please take your food (and leave).
example_zh: 我走路去的餐厅。

name: 아/어 가다
meaning: Indicates an action that has started is still in progress but will soon end.
examples: 물이 조금밖에 안 남아서 거의 다 마셔 가요.
거의 다 도착해 가요. 조금만 더 기다려 주세요.
ko: 시작된 동작이 곧 끝나게 됨을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: The TV show is about to end.
There's only a bit of water left, so I'm almost done drinking it.
I'm almost done reading this book.
I'm almost there (about to arrive). Please wait a little longer.
example_zh: 电视剧快结束了。

name: 아/어 가지다
meaning: Used to indicate time order of 2 actions, that the 1st action must be completed in order to do the 2nd action.
ko: 앞의 동작을 끝낸 뒤 뒤의 동작을 함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I washed my clothes and am hanging them now.
I borrowed a book from my friend and read it.
example_zh: 把衣服洗了，现在正晾着。

name: 아/어 가지다
meaning: Used to indicate reason or cause to do an action.
examples: 낮에 커피를 많이 마셔 가지고 밤에 잠을 못잤어요.
ko: 어떤 행동을 하는 이유나 원인을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I am so full because I ate a lot.
I drank a lot of coffee during the day, so couldn't sleep at night.
example_zh: 吃得太多，肚子好撑。

name: 아/어 나가다
meaning: Marks an action as ongoing or in progress.
examples: 아무것도 없어도 너만 있으면 살아 나가겠지.
우리 아들이 일을 열심히 해나가고 있어.
ko: 동작이 계속 진행됨을 나타내는 보조 용언.
example_en: Even if I don't have anything, if I just have you I can keep on living.
Our son keeps working hard.
example_zh: 就算什么都没有，只要有你我就能活下去。

name: 아/어 내다
meaning: Marks an action as completed through much difficulty, effort, or time.
examples: 김치리더 덕분에 드디어 그 어려운 책을 읽어 냈습니다!
ko: 어려움을 견디고 마침내 해 냄을 나타내는 보조 용언.
example_en: Thanks to Kimchi Reader, I finally read that difficult book.
The policeman finally found the culprit.
example_zh: 多亏了这个阅读工具，我终于啃完了那本难懂的书！

name: 아/어 놓다
meaning: Indicates the continuation of a state after an action is being done or just maintaining a certain state.
examples: 음식 냄새가 많이 나서 창문을 열어 놨어요.
밖이 갑자기 어두워지고 저는 겁이 나서 커튼을 닫아 놓았어요.
ko: 동작이 끝난 상태가 유지됨을 나타내는 보조 용언.
example_en: The smell of food was strong, so I opened the window.
It suddenly got dark outside, and I was scared, so I closed the curtain.
I put the key in the drawer.
example_zh: 饭菜味很大，所以我把窗户打开了。

name: 아/어 달다
meaning: Asking for the act previously mentioned to be carried out.
examples: 친구가 갑자기 큰돈을 빌려 달라는데 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠어.
아이는 잘못했다며 한 번만 용서해 달라고 아버지께 빌고 있었다.
ko: 남에게 자기를 위해 어떤 행동을 해 달라고 청할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: My friend suddenly asked me to lend him a lot of money, and I don't know what to do.
The child was begging his father to forgive him just once, saying he was wrong.
example_zh: 朋友突然要我借他一大笔钱，我不知道该怎么办。

name: 아/어 달라고
meaning: Used to pass along what the speaker has requested for another person to do something for them.
ko: 부탁을 간접적으로 전할 때 쓰는 인용 표현.
example_en: Dad asked you to take out the trash (for him).
My younger brother asked me to help him.
example_zh: 爸爸让我把垃圾扔了。

name: 아/어 대다
meaning: This expression is used to show that something is done too much and keeps happening.
examples: 동생이 계속 울어 대서 머리가 아파요.
고양이가 밤에 울어 대서 잠을 못 잤어요.
ko: 성의 없이 자꾸 되풀이함을 나타내는 보조 용언.
example_en: My younger sibling kept crying too much, so I have a headache.
The cat kept crying at night, so I couldn't sleep.
example_zh: 弟妹一直哭个不停，我头都疼了。

name: 아/어 두다
meaning: Indicates the continuation of a state after an action is being done or just maintaining a certain state.
examples: 서랍 안에 중요한 것이 많아서 항상 잠가 둡니다.
ko: 동작을 끝낸 상태로 두었음을 나타내는 보조 용언.
example_en: There are many important things in the drawer, so I always lock it.
Hang the coat on this hanger.
I bought a lot of ramen.
example_zh: 抽屉里有很多重要的东西，所以我总是锁着。

name: 아/어 두다
meaning: Doing an action in advance to prepare for a future event.
examples: 발표할 때 실수하지 않으려면 연습을 많이 해 두세요.
ko: 동작을 끝낸 상태로 두었음을 나타내는 보조 용언.
example_en: If you don't want to make a mistake during the presentation, practice a lot in advance.
example_zh: 要想发表时不出错，就要提前多加练习。

name: 아/어 드리다
meaning: Indicate that you are doing something for the sake of others or to ask someone to do something for you.
examples: 고객님, 이 상품이 마음에 드시면 새 상품으로 포장해 드릴게요.
ko: 남을 위해 행동함을 높여 나타내는 보조 용언.
example_en: Do you want me to turn on the air conditioner?
Sir, if you like this product, I will wrap it as a new product for you.
example_zh: 要我帮您开空调吗？

name: 아/어 마지않다
meaning: Emphasizes that an action is being done sincerely.
examples: 올해는 좋은 일만 있으시길 바라 마지않습니다.
그대를 기대해마지않아 자꾸 먼 바다를 쳐다보오!
ko: 진심으로 몹시,라는 느낌을 나타내는 보조 용언.
example_en: I sincerely wish you only the best this year.
I stare at the distant sea, sincerely waiting for you.
Hyunwoo really loves Subin.
example_zh: 衷心祝愿您今年只有好事发生。

name: 아/어 버리다
meaning: Used after an action or event is finished and completed. It can refers to facts nothing remains after that or the speaker's feeling about it.
ko: 동작이 완전히 끝났거나 아쉬움·안도의 느낌을 더하는 보조 용언.
example_en: That person finally left. (And so I feel relieved)
I quit smoking for my health.
example_zh: 那个人终于离开了。（如释重负）

name: 아/어 보다
meaning: Expresses the meaning of trying something out or experiencing an action.
ko: 일단 해 봄으로써 경험함을 나타내는 보조 용언.
example_en: Try eating kimchi.
Shall I try reading it once?
example_zh: 请尝尝泡菜。

name: 아/어 보이다
meaning: Conveys feelings based on some outward appearance.
examples: 마크 씨, 얼굴이 피곤해 보여요. 무슨 일 있어요?
도서관 앞에서 봤는데 많이 우울해 보였어요.
이 음식은 많이 매워 보이는데 괜찮아요?
ko: 겉으로 드러난 모습에서 느껴짐을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Mark, you look tired. Did something happen?
I saw him in front of the library, and he looked really sad.
This food looks really spicy. Are you okay?
example_zh: 马克，你看起来很疲惫。发生什么事了吗？

name: 아/어 봤자
meaning: Indicates that even if the first clause is true, it is no use or ineffective. The second clause is negative and often expresses a reason that the first clause is in vain.
examples: 울지 마. 울어봤자 해결되는 거 하나도 없어.
지금 바로 헬스 끊어봤자 당분간 꾸준히 다닐 시간 없을 것 같아.
이런 불편한 회식자리에 오래 남아봤자 신경질만 낼 거야.
ko: 해 봤자 소용없음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I've found that <f>even</f> if you have a lot of money or influence, it's futile.
Don't cry. Crying doesn't fix anything <f>(regardless)</f>.
<f>Even if</f> I sign up for a gym membership right now, I won't have the time to properly work out for the time being.
<f>If</f> I stay longer at this uncomfortable hweshik, I'll just lose my temper.
example_zh: 我发现就算有很多权力或钱，也都是徒劳。

name: 아/어 빠지다
meaning: Indicate becoming completely absorbed or immersed in the action or state.
examples: 그 그림이 너무 아름다워서 바라봐 빠져버렸어요.
소설이 너무 흥미로워서 밤새 읽어 빠졌어요.
그는 최근 도예를 빚어 빠져서 하루 종일 흙을 다루고 있어요.
게임을 해 빠져 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
그녀는 요가를 연습해 빠져서 매일 열심히 운동하고 있어요.
그녀는 메이크업 튜토리얼을 봐 빠져서 매일 새로운 화장법을 시도해요.
로맨스 소설을 읽어 빠져서 휴대폰을 볼 시간도 없어요.
유럽 디저트 레시피를 만들어 빠져보니 이제 매주 새로운 케이크를 구워요.
그녀는 방탄소년단 영상을 봐 빠져 하루 종일 유튜브를 시청하고 있어요.
새로운 스킨케어 제품 정보를 찾아 빠져 밤늦게까지 인터넷을 뒤지고 있어요.
최신 패션 트렌드를 연구해 빠져 옷장 정리에 많은 시간을 쓰고 있어요.
인테리어 블로그를 보고 꾸며 빠져 집 안 분위기를 완전히 바꾸고 싶어 해요.
한복 디자인에 관심을 갖고 자료를 찾아 빠져 전통문화를 더 깊이 이해하게 되었어요.
ko: 그 상태에 완전히 빠졌음을 강조하는 보조 용언.
example_en: The painting was so beautiful that I became completely absorbed in looking at it.
The novel was so fascinating that I stayed up all night, completely absorbed in reading it.
He’s recently become so immersed in pottery that he spends the entire day working with clay.
I got so absorbed in playing the game that I completely lost track of time.
She’s so deeply involved in practicing yoga that she works out diligently every day.
She’s become so absorbed in makeup tutorials that she tries a new style every day.
She’s so engrossed in reading romance novels that she doesn’t even have time to check her phone.
After becoming completely absorbed in making European dessert recipes, she now bakes a new cake every week.
She’s so into watching BTS videos that she spends the whole day on YouTube.
Having gotten completely immersed in looking up new skincare products, she stays up late browsing the internet.
She’s become so absorbed in studying the latest fashion trends that she spends a lot of time reorganizing her wardrobe.
After getting deeply absorbed in interior design blogs, she wants to completely change her home’s atmosphere.
Becoming interested in hanbok design and getting absorbed in researching it, she gained a deeper understanding of traditional culture.
example_zh: 那幅画太美了，我看得入了迷。

name: 아/어 오다
meaning: Indicates an action that started in the past continues into the present.
ko: 과거에 시작된 동작이 현재까지 이어짐을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I've lived in Korea as of 10 years ago (so far even till now now)
I always believe in my teacher (before and still to this day).
I've worked hard (from the start continually even now)
I've waited for ths moment.
example_zh: 我从10年前起一直在韩国生活到现在。

name: 아/어 오다
meaning: Indicates an action comes from a destination/person or moves towards the speaker's current location.
examples: 치킨을 먹고 싶어? 그럼 지금 사 올게.
ko: 동작이 다른 곳에서 말하는 사람 쪽으로 옴을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: You want to eat some fried chicken? Then I'll go buy some now (and then come back here).
The students came into the classroom.
Bring (to me) a few books.
example_zh: 想吃炸鸡？那我现在去买回来。

name: 아/어 있다
meaning: Expresses a continuing state of a completed action. The action has been completed, but the state still maintains itself.
examples: 버스 정류장에는 사람들이 줄을 서 있어요.
ko: 동작이 끝난 뒤의 상태가 유지됨을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: The wound is still there on the face.
People are standing in line at the bus stop.
example_zh: 脸上的伤还留着。

name: 아/어 주다
meaning: Indicate that you are doing something for the sake of others or to ask someone to do something for you.
examples: 여러분 벌써 포기하지 말아주세요! 제가 천천히 설명해 보겠습니다!
ko: 남을 위해 행동함을 나타내는 보조 용언.
example_en: The grandfather put the fish in the river.
Please don't give up yet! I will explain it slowly!
example_zh: 爷爷把鲤鱼放回了江里。

name: 아/어 지다
meaning: Express a change in state over time. Can only be used with descriptive verbs.
examples: 요즘 운동을 해서 살이 많이 빠졌어요.
공부를 하고 있는데 갑자기 방에 불이 꺼졌어요.
ko: 상태가 점차 변해감을 나타내는 보조 용언(형용사에 쓰임).
example_en: I've lost a lot of weight recently because I've been exercising.
I was studying when the lights suddenly went out.
example_zh: 最近坚持运动，瘦了很多。

name: 아/어 하다
meaning: Added to descriptive verbs to change turn them into action verbs and convey an emotion or sensation.
ko: 감정이나 느낌을 나타내는 보조 용언(제3자에게 쓰임).
example_en: My younger sibling seems to enjoy studying Korean.
I dislike people who are insensitive.
example_zh: 弟妹觉得学韩语很有意思。

name: 아/어도 되다
meaning: Used to ask for permission or approval before doing a certain action
ko: 허락을 구하거나 허용을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: May I take a picture?
May I sit here?
Do you mind if I open the window?
example_zh: 可以拍照吗？

name: 안 아요
meaning: A pattern used to express the negative form of a verb.
ko: '안'을 써서 동사를 부정하는 구어 표현.
example_en: I don't like fish.
I called you earlier, why didn't you pick up?
example_zh: 我不喜欢鱼。

name: 아/어야 되다/하다
meaning: Express an obligation or necessity to do something.
examples: 내일 시험이 있어요. 그래서 공부해야 돼요.
감기에 걸리지 않기 위해서 따뜻한 옷을 입어야 해요.
늘 너무 피곤해요. 집에서 쉬어야 돼요.
ko: 의무나 필요를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I have an exam tomorrow. So I must study.
You should wear warm clothes to avoid catching a cold.
I am so tired today. I have to rest at home.
example_zh: 明天有考试，所以必须学习。

name: 았/었으면 좋겠다
meaning: Expresses a person's wish or hope about something that has yet to be realized.
examples: 친구들하고 스키장에 갈거예요. 방학이 빨리 왔으면 좋겠어요.
ko: 아직 이루어지지 않은 소망을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: It would be nice to get married in the warm spring.
I plan to go skiing with my friends. I wish vacation would come sooner.
I wish I had a car.
I hope it snows on Christmas.
example_zh: 希望能在温暖的春天结婚。

name: (았/었/했)을 것
meaning: Indicates an assumption about past events or potential outcomes of past events.
examples: 날씨가 좀 더 따뜻했다면 나갔을 거예요.
ko: 과거의 일에 대한 추측을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: If the weather was a little warmer, I would have gone out.
I would have bought that camera if it were cheaper.
The child must have had a stomachache.
example_zh: 要是天气再暖和一点，我就出去了。

name: 에 대해(서)
meaning: When you want to talk about something
examples: 한국 패션 스타일에 대해 어떻게 생각해요?
ko: 어떤 것에 관하여 이야기할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: What do you think about Korean fashion style?
People talk a lot about traveling.
example_zh: 你觉得韩国的时尚风格怎么样？

name: 에 따라(서)
meaning: Used to say depending on something.
examples: 날씨에 따라 옷을 고르는 것이 달라요.
ko: 어떤 것에 좇아 달라짐을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Bring an umbrella depending on the weather.
People's choices vary depending on the price.
The choice of clothes varies depending on the weather.
example_zh: 根据天气情况带伞。

name: 에 비해(서)/비하면
meaning: Used to compare two items.
examples: 택시를 타는 거에 비해 기차를 타는 건 더 싸요.
우리 아버지가 사진에 비하면 실물이 훨씬 낫거든요.
ko: 두 대상을 비교할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Taking the train is much cheaper than taking a taxi.
My father looks better in real life compared to the pictures.
example_zh: 坐火车比坐出租车便宜。

name: 에도 불구하고
meaning: Expresses that something occurs despite a certain situation or condition.
ko: 어떤 상황에도 그 결과가 그대로 나타남을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Despite the rain, he went to work.
Despite being tired, he continued studying.
Despite the difficulties, she did not give up.
In spite of failure, she tried again.
example_zh: 尽管下雨，他还是去上班了。

name: (으)나 마나
meaning: Express that doing something will not change the result; it's pointless to do it.
examples: 지금 가나 마나 그녀는 없을 거예요.
그 영화는 보나 마나 재미없을 거야.
그 책은 읽으나 마나 시간 낭비예요.
시험 공부를 하나 마나 결과는 똑같을 거야.
그 사람을 만나나 마나 시간 낭비예요.
하나 더 죽이나마나 손해 볼 거 없어! 어차피 무기징역이잖아. 어차피 못 나가는데.
ko: 해도 안 해도 결과가 같음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Even if you go now, she won't be there.
There's no point in watching that movie; it'll be boring.
There's no point in reading that book; it's a waste of time.
Whether you study for the exam or not, the result will be the same.
Meeting that person is a waste of time.
He has nothing to lose whether he kills another person or not! He's already in prison for life. He can't get out regardless.
There's no point cramming for a test. The result will be the same as if you didn't cram.
example_zh: 现在去不去，她都不会在。

name: (으)려고 하다
meaning: Express an intention, desire or purpose to do something. The speaker expresses one's intention to do the act mentioned in the preceding statement.
examples: 염색을 하려고 하는데 요즘 무슨 색이 유행이에요?
일월에 운동을 시작하려고 하는 사람들이 많아요.
ko: 행동하려는 의도를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I'm planning to dye my hair, what color is popular these days?
I'm going to the park because the weather is nice.
There are many people who intend to start exercising in January.
example_zh: 我打算染头发，最近流行什么颜色？

name: (으)려던 참이다
meaning: The speaker is just about to do something very soon.
ko: 마침 그러려던 참임을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: As I was just about to get on the train, I met him.
I am about to have dinner, want to join me?
example_zh: 正要上火车的时候遇到了他。

name: (으)로 인하다
meaning: Indicates the cause or reason for a certain situation or event.
examples: 지진으로 인해 많은 사람들이 피해를 입었습니다.
ko: 어떤 일의 원인이나 이유를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: The game was canceled due to rain.
The road was blocked because of an accident.
Many people were affected as a result of the earthquake.
The work was delayed because of computer problems.
example_zh: 比赛因下雨取消了。

name: (으)면 안 되다
meaning: Used to say a particular action is not allowed.
ko: 그렇게 해서는 안 됨을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Smoking indoors is not allowed.
Using the phone while driving is not allowed.
You may not cross the street now.
example_zh: 室内禁止吸烟。

name: (으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다
meaning: Indicates you have a certain experience in the past.
examples: 어릴 때 병원에 입원한 적이 있어요.
ko: 과거의 경험이 있거나 없음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I was hospitalized when I was a child.
I've made a mistake because of my poor Korean.
example_zh: 我小时候住过院。

name: (으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다
meaning: Indicates you not having a certain experience in the past
examples: 어릴 때 병원에 입원한 적이 없어요.
ko: 과거의 경험이 있거나 없음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I have never been late to work.
I have never been hospitalised when I was a child.
example_zh: 我上班从没迟到过。

name: (으)ㄴ 지
meaning: Indicates how much time has passed since some situation or action occurred
examples: 담배 끊은 지 한 달 됐어요.
ko: 그 일이 있은 지 얼마나 지났는지를 나타내는 표현.
example_en: It's been two years since I came to Korea.
It's been one month since I stopped smoking.
It's been over five hours since you started playing computer games.
example_zh: 我来韩国已经两年了。

name: (으)ㄴ 채로
meaning: Used to indicate that the following clause is performed whilst in the state or condition described before.
ko: 어떤 상태 그대로 뒤 동작을 함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Enter the water with clothes on.
The package was delivered unopened.
example_zh: 穿着衣服下水。

name: ㄹ/을 길이 없다
meaning: There is no possible way or method to do something
examples: 죽은 그 사람이 누구인지 알 길이 없어요.
우리가 언제 그 일을 끝낼지 알 길이 없어요.
ko: 그렇게 할 방법이 전혀 없음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: There is no way of verifying that fact.
There is no way of knowing who that dead person is.
There is no way to solve this problem.
There is no way to uncover the truth.
There is no way of knowing when we will finish that work.
example_zh: 那个事实无从确认。

name: ㄹ/을 리가 없다
meaning: Indicates the speaker's disbelief or doubt
examples: 이 음식을 안 좋아할 리가 없어요.
ko: 그럴 가능성을 믿기지 않을 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: There's no way my friend would be late.
There's no way you won't like this food.
example_zh: 朋友不可能迟到。

name: 을/를 막론하고
meaning: Indicates that the noun is not considered in making a judgment or decision; regardless of noun
examples: 경험을 막론하고 누구나 참여할 수 있어요.
ko: 어떤 경우에도 상관없음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: You can apply regardless of gender.
The event will proceed as scheduled regardless of the weather.
Everyone is welcome regardless of nationality.
This place is beautiful regardless of the season.
Anyone can participate regardless of experience.
example_zh: 不分性别都可以报名。

name: (으)ㄹ 만하다
meaning: Indicates something is worth doing
ko: 할 가치가 있거나 할 만함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: This movie is really worth watching.
Korean is worth studying.
example_zh: 这部电影真的值得一看。

name: (으)ㄹ 바에야
meaning: Used when expressing a preference between two choices, where neither is ideal. The first choice is either not feasible or inappropriate, so the second choice is selected instead.
examples: 그 영화를 볼 바에야 차라리 책을 읽겠어요.
혼자 갈 바에야 친구랑 같이 가는 게 낫겠어요.
ko: 둘 중 차라리 뒤쪽을 택하겠다는 뜻을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Rather than watching that movie, I would prefer to read a book.
If I have to go alone, it's better to go with a friend.
example_zh: 与其看那部电影，我宁可读书。

name: (으)ㄹ 뿐만 아니라
meaning: Shows that one does A and also does B
examples: 정원에 점핑스파이더가 많을 뿐만 아니라 애완동물로도 키워요.
내 여자친구는 예쁠 뿐만 아니라 똑똑해요.
그는 음악을 잘 연주할 뿐만 아니라 노래도 잘 불러요.
ko: 앞 내용에 더해 뒤 내용도 있음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Not only do I have a lot of jumping spiders in my yard, I also have one as a pet.
My girlfriend is not only beautiful, but also smart.
He not only plays music well, but also sings well.
example_zh: 院子里不仅有好多跳蛛，我还养了一只当宠物。

name: (으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다
meaning: Used when there is no other choice but the preceding state/action.
examples: 너무 빨리 운전해서, 차 손잡이를 꽉 잡을 수밖에 없었다.
금연법이 시행되면 PC방을 닫을 수밖에 없다.
ko: 다른 선택이 없어 그렇게 할 수밖에 없음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: They were driving so fast I had no choice but to grip the car handle tightly.
If the law comes into effect, I will have no other option but to shut down the shop
example_zh: 车开得太快，我只好紧紧抓住车把手。

name: 을/를 위해(서)
meaning: Used when doing something to achieve a goal or for a specific purpose.
examples: 건강을 위해서 매일 비타민을 먹고 있어요.
ko: 목표나 목적을 위해 행동함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Soldiers are people who work for their country.
I take vitamins daily for my health.
example_zh: 军人是为国家工作的人。

name: (으)ㄹ 정도로
meaning: Expresses degree of an action
ko: 그만큼의 정도에 이름을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I worked so much that I am extremely tired.
It was so funny that I laughed until I cried.
example_zh: 工作太多，累得不行。

name: (으)ㄹ 정도이다
meaning: Expresses the degree or extent of a state or action, showing that something is so [adjective/verb] that a certain result follows.
examples: 그 영화는 너무 감동적이어서 눈물이 계속 흘렀을 정도였어요.
이 음식은 너무 맛있어서 매일 먹고 싶을 정도예요.
밖이 너무 추워서 아무것도 할 수 없을 정도였어요.
ko: 그 정도로 심하거나 뛰어남을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: He is so tired that he could collapse.
The movie was so moving that tears kept flowing.
This food is so delicious that I want to eat it every day.
It was so cold outside that I couldn't do anything.
example_zh: 他累得都快晕倒了。

name: (으)ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다
meaning: Used to say you know or have the ability to do something.
examples: 저는 잡채하고 스파게티를 만들 줄 알아요.
ko: 어떤 일을 할 줄 아는 능력을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I know how to cook a tasty doenjang stew.
I know how to make japchae and spaghetti.
example_zh: 我会做大酱汤，而且做得很好喝。

name: (으)ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다
meaning: Used to say you don't know or don't have the ability to do something.
examples: 휴대 전화로 사진을 보낼 줄 몰라요.
ko: 어떤 일을 할 줄 아는 능력을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I don't know how to dsend pictures by mobile phone.
I don't know how to speak English.
example_zh: 我不会用手机发照片。

name: (으)ㄹ 테니(까)
meaning: The second part of the sentence gives the speaker's advice or suggestion to the listener. The first part explains why the speaker is giving that advice or suggestion. '까' is sometimes omitted.
examples: 비가 올 테니까 우산을 가져 가세요.
일찍 일어날 테니까 늦지 말고 잘 준비하세요.
바쁠 테니까 오늘은 점심을 밖에서 먹자.
요리는 내가 할 테니 청소기 좀 돌려.
ko: 화자의 추측을 근거로 상대에게 권유할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Since it will rain, please bring an umbrella.
Since you will wake up early, don't be late and prepare well.
Since we'll be busy, let's eat out for lunch today.
I'm going to make the food, so you vacuum.
example_zh: 要下雨了，带上伞吧。

name: (으)ㄹ 텐데
meaning: Used to express an expected or intended future event.
examples: 내일 비가 올 텐데 우산을 챙겨 가세요.
지금쯤 도착했을 텐데 아직 오지 않았어.
일찍 일어날 텐데 왜 아직도 자고 있어요?
ko: 예상되는 상황을 배경으로 제시할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: It's probably going to rain tomorrow, so make sure to bring an umbrella.
They should have arrived by now, but they still haven't come.
You're supposed to wake up early, so why are you still sleeping?
example_zh: 明天可能会下雨，记得带伞。

name: (으)ㄹ까 말까
meaning: Express hesitation or indecision about doing something.
examples: 오늘 학교에 갈까 말까 생각 중이에요.
배가 안 고파서 점심을 먹을까 말까 해요.
나는 차를 살까 말까 장난스럽게 생각하고 있어요.
새로운 취미를 시작할까 말까 고민하고 있어요.
ko: 할까 말까 망설여짐을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I'm thinking about whether to go to school today or not.
I'm wondering whether to eat lunch since I'm not hungry.
I'm playfully considering whether to buy a car or not.
I'm debating whether to start a new hobby or not.
I'm hesitating about whether to call my friend or not.
example_zh: 我在想要不要去学校。

name: (으)ㄹ까 봐
meaning: Indicates the speaker did, or is doing, something in the second clause because they are worried or afraid that what is mentioned in the first clause has happened or will happen.
examples: 중요한 일을 잊어버릴까 봐 수첩에 항상 메모해요.
살이 찔까 봐 기름진 음식 안 먹어요.
ko: 염려되는 마음에 그렇게 함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I am worried that the weather would be bad in weekend
I always write memo because I am afraid that I would forget important things.
I don't eat fatty food since I am worried that I would gain weight.
example_zh: 担心周末天气不好。

name: (으)ㄹ까 하다
meaning: The speaker is not sure about their plan or intention, and it might change.
examples: 이번 방학에는 한국 여행을 할까 해요.
ko: 확실하지 않은 계획이 있음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I'm thinking about eating pizza tonight.
I'm thinking of taking a trip to Korera this vacation
example_zh: 我在想要不要今晚吃披萨。

name: (으)ㄹ락 말락
meaning: Expresses that an action is about to happen or really close to occurring with no indication of it actually happening or not.
examples: 비가 올락 말락 하는 날씨가 제일 싫거든요.
남편이 설득될락 말락 해서 조금 더 기다려줘.
요즘은 눈이 너무 올랑 말랑 하네요.
ko: 일이 일어날 듯 말 듯 한계에 이르렀음을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I hate it when it seems like it will rain.
My husband is this close to being persuaded so just wait a bit more.
It seems like it will snow any minute now.
example_zh: 我最讨厌这种要下不下的天气。

name: (으)ㄹ지(도) 모르다
meaning: Used to indicate that something might happen or could possibly occur.
examples: 바람이 많이 불어서 비행기가 출발할 수 있을지 모르겠습니다.
ko: 어쩌면 그럴지도 모른다는 가능성을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: It might rain this afternoon.
I don't know if the plane can take off because it's very windy.
example_zh: 今天下午可能会下雨。

name: 전에
meaning: Used to say before a certain time or before an action
ko: 어떤 시간이나 동작의 앞임을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I came to Korea 5 years ago.
Please take this medicine before meals.
example_zh: 我5年前来的韩国。

name: 중
meaning: Indicate that the subject is in the process of performing an action
ko: 동작이 진행되고 있는 중임을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: I am in class now. I will call you later.
That building is under construction.
example_zh: 我正在上课，稍后给你打电话。

name: 지 그렇다
meaning: Used as -지 그래, -지 그래요, -지 그러세요 depending on the level of speech to suggest that the listener do something. -지 그래 and -지 그래요 are less direct / more gentle compared to other kinds of suggestions in 반말 and 존댓말 respectively, but -지 그러세요 is probably on the more direct side and should not be used to those above you.
examples: 그 단어를 모르면 사전에 찾아보지 그래요?
식당 구석에 저 의자 좀 치우지 그래요? 너무 낡아서 눈에 거슬려요.
ko: 그러게 그렇게 하지,라며 상대를 권할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: If you don't know that word, how about you look it up?
Can you please put that chair in the corner of the restaurant away? It's so old, I don't like seeing it.
Can we get going now?
example_zh: 不知道那个单词的话，查查词典怎么样？

name: 지 말다
meaning: Used to requesting, persuading or ordering the listener not to do something.
examples: 선생님이 내일 시험을 보니까 시험 시간에 늦지 말라고 했어요.
ko: 하지 말라고 만류하거나 명령할 때 쓰는 표현.
example_en: Don't expect anything.
Don't run in the hallway.
The teacher told me not to be late for the exam tomorrow.
example_zh: 别指望什么。

name: 지 못하다
meaning: A pattern to expresses the subject's inability to do something or the fact that something does not go according to the subject's will.
examples: 우리는 삼 일 동안 협상하였지만, 거래를 하지 못했습니다.
ko: 능력이 없거나 여건이 안 되어 못함을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: My younger sibling cannot skate.
We negotiated for three days, but we couldn't make a deal.
example_zh: 我的弟妹不会滑冰。

name: 지 않다
meaning: A pattern used to express the negative form of a verb.
examples: 돈이 부족해서 살 만한 집을 구하기가 쉽지 않아요.
ko: 동사의 부정을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: You don't have to submit the report by today.
It's not easy to find an appropriate house to live in because of the lack of money.
example_zh: 报告不必今天交。

name: 지 않아도 되다
meaning: Used to say a particular behaviour is not necessary. It is the negative form of <f>아/어야 되다</f>.
examples: 유치원생은 버스 요금을 내지 않아도 돼요.
평일이니까 영화 표를 미리 사지 않아도 돼요.
ko: 그렇게 하지 않아도 됨을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: Preschool students don't have to pay the bus fare.
Because it's a weekday, we don't have to buy tickets in advance.
example_zh: 幼儿园学生不用交公交车费。

name: 후에/뒤에
meaning: Used to say something happens after a certain period of time
ko: 일정한 시간이나 동작 다음임을 나타내는 표현.
example_en: My baby will be born one month later.
I got a job after college graduation.
example_zh: 宝宝一个月后出生。

name: 'ㄷ' 불규칙
meaning: the 'ㄷ' irregular conjugation: ㄷ changes to ㄹ before vowel endings
examples: 날씨가 좋은데 밖에 나가서 좀 걸을까요?
이 노래 들어 봤어요? 정말 좋아요.
example_zh: 我一边听音乐一边运动。
我没钱，所以走着去了。
我问了那个女人的电话号码。
天气很好，我们出去散散步怎么样？
你听过这首歌吗？真的很好。
example_en: I listen to music while I exercise.
I had no money, so I went by foot.
I asked her for her phone number.
The weather's nice, so why don't we go for a walk outside?
Have you heard this song? It's really good.
zh: 'ㄷ'不规则活用：部分词干以ㄷ结尾的动词后接元音开头的词尾时，ㄷ变为ㄹ
ko: 일부 어간이 'ㄷ'으로 끝나는 동사에 모음으로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㄷ'이 'ㄹ'로 바뀌는 불규칙 활용.
notes: Although the stems of 닫다 (to close), 받다 (to receive), and 믿다 (to believe) end in ㄷ, they are conjugated regularly.
formation: 어간 끝 'ㄷ' + 모음으로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㄹ'로 변함 (예: 듣다→들어요, 묻다→물어요, 걷다→걸어요)

name: 'ㄹ' 불규칙
meaning: the 'ㄹ' irregular conjugation: ㄹ is dropped before endings beginning with ㄴ, ㅂ, or ㅅ
examples: 백화점이 몇 시에 여는지 알고 싶어요.
전자 사전을 어디에서 싸게 파는지 아세요?
우리 집은 머니까 학교 다니기 힘들어요.
example_zh: 孩子一个人玩得很好。
我想知道百货商店几点开门。
你现在做的是什么？
你知道哪里有卖便宜的电子词典吗？
我家离学校远，所以上学很辛苦。
example_en: The girl plays well by herself.
I'd like to know what time the department store opens.
What are you making?
Do you know where I can get an electronic dictionary for a good price?
Our house is far from school, so it's hard to commute.
zh: 'ㄹ'不规则活用：词干以ㄹ结尾时，后接ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ开头的词尾，ㄹ脱落
ko: 어간이 'ㄹ'로 끝나는 동사와 형용사에 'ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ'으로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㄹ'이 탈락하는 불규칙 활용.
notes: When -(으)ㄹ is added to stems ending in ㄹ, such as -(으)ㄹ 때, -(으)게요, and -(으)ㄹ 래요?, ㄹ is omitted and the stem attaches directly to the ending. e.g. 살다 + -(으)ㄹ 때 → 살 때; 만들다 + -(으)ㄹ 래요? → 만들래요?
formation: 어간 끝 'ㄹ' + 'ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ'로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㄹ' 탈락 (예: 살다→삽니다, 만들다→만드세요)

name: 'ㅂ' 불규칙
meaning: the 'ㅂ' irregular conjugation: ㅂ changes to 우 (or 오) before vowel endings
example_zh: 咖啡很烫，请小心。
天气冷，所以我待在家里了。
我喜欢吃辣的食物。
你喜欢什么样的电影？
菜有点淡，请给我点盐。
example_en: The coffee is hot, so be careful.
It's cold outside, so I stayed home.
I like spicy food.
What kind of movies do you like?
The food is a little bland, so could I have some salt?
zh: 'ㅂ'不规则活用：词干以ㅂ结尾时，后接元音开头的词尾，ㅂ变为우（돕다/곱다变为오）
ko: 어간이 'ㅂ'으로 끝나는 동사와 형용사에 모음으로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㅂ'이 '우'로 바뀌는 불규칙 활용('돕다/곱다'는 '오'로 바뀜).
notes: 돕다 (to assist) and 곱다 (lovely/charming) are the only two words that change ㅂ to 오; all others change to 우. Although the stems of 좁다, 입다, 씹다, and 잡다 end in ㅂ, they are conjugated regularly.
formation: 어간 끝 'ㅂ' + 모음으로 시작하는 어미 → '우'로 변함 (돕다/곱다는 '오'로 변함)

name: 'ㅅ' 불규칙
meaning: the 'ㅅ' irregular conjugation: ㅅ is dropped before vowel endings
examples: 컵에 커피와 크림, 설탕을 넣고 저어요.
example_zh: 被蚊子咬了，眼睛肿了。
在杯子里放入咖啡、奶油和糖，然后搅拌。
哪件衣服更好？
孩子的名字是谁起的？
感冒都好了吗？
example_en: A mosquito bit me, so my eye became swollen.
I put coffee, cream, and sugar in the cup and stir it all together.
Which outfit is better?
Who named your child?
Did you get over your cold?
zh: 'ㅅ'不规则活用：部分词干以ㅅ结尾时，后接元音开头的词尾，ㅅ脱落
ko: 일부 어간이 'ㅅ'으로 끝나는 동사와 형용사에 모음으로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㅅ'이 탈락하는 불규칙 활용.
notes: In Korean, vowels often combine when they meet (e.g. 배우 + -어요 → 배워요). However, in the case of irregular ㅅ stems, even though vowels may meet after the ㅅ is deleted, they do not combine. e.g. 짓다 + -어요 → 지어요 (O) / 저요 (X); 낫다 + -아요 → 나아요 (O) / 나요 (X). Also, although the stems of 벗다, 웃다, and 씻다 end in ㅅ, they are conjugated regularly.
formation: 어간 끝 'ㅅ' + 모음으로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㅅ' 탈락 (예: 짓다→지어요, 낫다→나아요)

name: 'ㅎ' 불규칙
meaning: the 'ㅎ' irregular conjugation: ㅎ is dropped before vowel endings (and the 아/어 ending becomes ㅐ)
examples: 왕비는 백설 공주에게 빨간 사과를 줬어요.
왕자는 크고 파란 눈으로 공주를 봤어요.
하늘은 파랗고 구름은 하애서 그림 같아요.
example_zh: 白雪公主头发乌黑，皮肤白皙。
王后给了白雪公主一个红苹果。
王子用又大又蓝的眼睛看着公主。
秋天的天空真蓝。
天空湛蓝，云朵洁白，就像一幅画。
example_en: Snow White has black hair and a white complexion.
The queen gave Snow White a red apple.
The prince looked at Snow White with his big blue eyes.
The autumn sky is really blue.
The sky is blue and the clouds are white, just like a painting.
zh: 'ㅎ'不规则活用：词干以ㅎ结尾的形容词后接元音开头的词尾时，ㅎ脱落（아/어类词尾变为ㅐ）
ko: 어간이 'ㅎ'으로 끝나는 형용사에 모음으로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㅎ'이 탈락하는 불규칙 활용.
notes: When the stems of 이렇다, 그렇다, 저렇다, and 어떻다 are added to endings that begin with -아/어, they conjugate to 이래, 그래, 저래, and 어때 instead of 이레, 그레, 저레, and 어레. Also, although the stems of 좋다, 많다, 낳다, and 넣다 end in ㅎ, they are conjugated regularly.
formation: 어간 끝 'ㅎ' + 모음으로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㅎ' 탈락 (아/어 계열은 'ㅐ'로 변함, 예: 하얗다→하얀/하얘요)

name: 'ㅡ' 불규칙
meaning: the 'ㅡ' irregular conjugation: ㅡ is dropped before endings beginning with 아/어
example_zh: 珉宇最近很忙。
请把灯关一下。
我肚子饿了。
电影太悲伤了，我正在哭。
天气不好，所以没能去郊游。
example_en: Minu is really busy these days.
Please turn off the lights.
I'm hungry.
I'm crying because the movie was so sad.
The weather was bad, so I couldn't go on the picnic.
zh: 'ㅡ'不规则活用：词干以ㅡ结尾时，后接아/어开头的词尾，ㅡ脱落
ko: 어간이 'ㅡ'로 끝나는 형용사와 동사에 '아/어'로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㅡ'가 탈락하는 불규칙 활용.
formation: 어간 끝 'ㅡ' + '아/어'로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㅡ' 탈락 (예: 바쁘다→바빠요, 예쁘다→예뻐서)

name: '르' 불규칙
meaning: the '르' irregular conjugation: ㅡ is dropped and ㄹ is added before 아/어 endings
examples: 댄 씨는 노래를 잘 불러서 인기가 많아요.
example_zh: 丹很会唱歌，所以很受欢迎。
上班时间地铁比公交车快。
我不会英语。
你剪头发了？真帅。
性格也很不一样。
example_en: Dane is popular because he can sing well.
The subway is faster than the bus during rush hour.
I don't speak English.
Did you cut your hair? It's stylish.
Their personalities are very different too.
zh: '르'不规则活用：词干以르结尾时，后接아/어开头的词尾，ㅡ脱落并添加ㄹ
ko: 어간이 '르'로 끝나는 동사와 형용사에 '아/어'로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㅡ'가 탈락하고 'ㄹ'이 덧나는 불규칙 활용.
formation: 어간 끝 '르' + '아/어'로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㅡ' 탈락 + 'ㄹ' 덧남 (예: 다르다→달라요, 부르다→불러요)

name: (으)네/-(으)ㄴ가 (하게체)
meaning: a slightly impolite speech style (하게체) used with people of a similar or younger age with whom one is on familiar terms
examples: 벌써 자네가 졸업할 때가 됐나? 세월이 빠르구먼, 서서 그러지 말고 앉아서 차라도 마시면서 이야기하세.
나는 집에 가는 길이네, 자네는 어디에 가나?
example_zh: 你已经到该毕业的时候了吗？岁月过得真快啊。别站着，坐下喝杯茶聊吧。
谢谢，你辛苦了。
真是好久不见。这里是我的房间。
我正在回家路上，你去哪儿？
喂，帮我一下这个。
example_en: Is it already time for you to graduate? My, how time flies. Don't just stand there—have a seat and let's talk over some tea or something.
Thank you. You've gone through a lot of effort.
It's been a really long time. This is my room.
I'm on my way home. Where are you going?
Hey, help me out with this.
zh: 略微降低对方的口吻（하게체），用于年龄相仿或较小、彼此关系亲近的对象。
ko: 듣는 사람이 말하는 사람과 나이가 비슷하거나 아랫사람인 경우에, 친숙한 사이라서 그 사람을 약간 낮춰 표현하는 말투입니다.
notes: For declarative sentences, adjectives take -(으)이 and nouns take (이)일세. The speaker refers to himself/herself as 나 and to the other person as 자네; when addressing the other person, 이보게 or 여보게 is mainly used. For the interrogative of verbs, both -나? and -는가? are possible.
formation: 동사 어간에 -네(평서), -(으)ㄴ가?/-나?(의문), -게(명령), -세(청유), -는구먼(감탄)을 붙임. 과거는 -았네/었네, 미래/추측은 -겠네. 형용사에는 -(으)이, 명사에는 (이)일세를 쓰기도 함.

name: 오/-(으)소 (하오체)
meaning: a slightly polite speech style (하오체) used with people of a similar or younger age whom one does not know well; mainly used in written signs and public notices
examples: 지금 몇 시오? 배가 고프니 식사하러 갑시다.
나는 잠깐 화장실에 갔다 오겠소, 그동안 무엇을 드실지 생각하고 계시오.
나는 제주도 사람이오. 당신은 어디에서 왔소?
example_zh: 现在几点了？我饿了，去吃饭吧。
我去一下洗手间，这期间您想想吃什么。
我是济州岛人。您从哪里来？
恕我冒昧，您是哪位？
请勿拍照。
example_en: What time is it now? I'm hungry, so let's go get something to eat.
I'm going to the restroom. In the meantime, think about what you want to eat.
I'm from Jeju Island. Where did you come from?
Excuse me, but who are you?
Do not take photographs.
zh: 略微尊敬对方的口吻（하오체），用于年龄相仿或较小、彼此不熟或不亲近的对象，多见于标牌、告示等书面语。
ko: 듣는 사람이 말하는 사람과 나이가 비슷하거나 아랫사람인 경우에, 서로 잘 모르거나 그리 친하지 않아 그 사람을 약간 높여 표현하는 말투입니다.
notes: In the imperative both -(으)오 and -(으)시오 are possible. A softer imperative can be made by adding the exclamatory ending -구려 to verb stems (e.g. 늦었으니 어서 가구려). In spoken language -오 is often pronounced -우 (e.g. 지금 어디에 가는 길이우?).
formation: 동사 어간에 받침이 없으면 -오, 받침이 있으면 -소(또는 -으오)를 붙임. 과거/완료는 -았소/었소, 미래/추측은 -겠소/이겠소, 의문형은 -(으)오?, 명령형은 -(으)오/-(으)시오, 감탄형은 -구려를 사용함.

name: 기가 이를 데 없다
meaning: to emphasize that the degree of some state of affairs defies description, being great, immense, or tremendous
examples: 그동안 많은 도움을 주셨는데 이런 일로 폐를 끼치게 되어 죄송스럽기가 이틀 데 없네요.
여러 나라 사람들이 모여 사는 도시답게 식당에서 파는 음식들도 다양하기 이를 매가 없었다.
지켜보는 관중 하나 없는 경기장은 쓸쓸하기 이를 대 없었지만 선수들은 최선을 다해 경기에 임했다.
가: 지난 주말에 '명성황후'라는 오페라를 봤는데 배우들의 연기가 훈륭하기가 이를 데 없었어요.
나: 그래요? 저도 보고 싶던 공연인데요. 무대 규모도 엄청나다면서요?
example_zh: 您一直帮了我们那么多，却因为这种事给您添麻烦，实在是非常抱歉。
不愧是世界各地的人们聚居的城市，餐厅里卖的饮食也丰富得无以复加。
没有一个观众的赛场冷清得难以形容，但选手们还是全力以赴地投入了比赛。
A：上周末看了歌剧《明成皇后》，演员们的演技好得没话说。
B：是吗？那也是我一直想看的演出。听说舞台规模也很宏大？
example_en: You've helped us out so much already, so I'm extremely sorry for inconveniencing you over this kind of matter.
